types.name: AllowanceEdit
types.doc: A change to one stated transmission allowance.

types.name: AssemblyBomMass
types.doc: BOM-only mass is a point-mass estimate, fixed or attached to a member.

types.name: AssemblyComponents
types.doc: The assembly package's component recipes.

types.name: AssemblyIntegrity
types.doc:
Checks that an assembly is physically put together, whatever machine it is:

- **support**: the two members of every mate touch, and every member is held up by the ground through mates whose
members touch, so a part "fixed" to something it does not reach is found;
- **rest interference**: no two members share volume at rest, members of one rigid body included, except where the
model says they mesh: a lead screw in its nut, a belt on its pulley or in its clamp, a chain on its sprocket, and
gear and rack teeth up to `meshOverlapLimit`. Nothing is excused by a hand-written list; a shaft in a bore must fit;
- **sweeps**: bodies that move relative to each other stay clear at sampled joint states (see `sweepStates`). A
sampled sweep, not a swept volume: a collision between samples can be missed;
- **drive consistency**: each transmission's coupling agrees with its parts' geometry. The root leader is moved a
little and the parts' material points are compared: a pinion's pitch point stays on its rack, meshing gears'
pitch circles roll on each other, and a nut travels one signed lead per turn of its screw (the thread's hand
included). A wrong ratio or sense is found here. Belts and chains are not checked this way: their strands are not
part geometry.

types.name: AssemblyInventory
types.doc:
One level's BOM lines beyond its members (hoses, wire, consumables), each with an optional point
mass, and the mass and BOM of a flattened assembly.

fields.name: massProperties
fields.doc: Posed component masses and BOM point masses; BOM lines with no mass model are listed apart.

types.name: AssemblyPreview

fields.name: scene
fields.doc: Scene of `assembly` in millimetres, with its joints and initial pose; `assemblyId` names the definition.

fields.name: preserveOwnership
fields.doc: Preserve include scopes and component metadata from the flattened export.

fields.name: shareDefinitions
fields.doc:
Points every occurrence at its shared definition (`definitionByOccurrence`; an occurrence missing
from it keeps its own) and drops the definitions nothing points at any more. A kept definition
takes the connectors of every occurrence that shares it; two occurrences may name the same
connector only with the same frame, since the scene holds one frame per name.

fields.name: part
fields.doc:
One scene part: tessellated mesh, material colour and mass properties. Closes `part`. The mesh
`maxGeometricFaces` bounds automatic face-mate descriptors (0 keeps all); explicit
assembly connectors and the complete mesh remain available. The mesh
deviates from the solid by a small fraction of its size, or by at most `deflection` (in the part's
units) when given, for a mesh that is measured against rather than only looked at.

types.name: AxisBuilder
types.doc: Shared member placement and rail travel for assemblies built from linear axes.

fields.name: zeroPoses
fields.doc: Poses with all axes at zero; these determine the mate connectors.

fields.name: overtravel
fields.doc: Room beyond travel before each guide block reaches its rail's end.

fields.name: axisDirection
fields.doc: The world direction axis `id` moves its block as its coordinate grows (see `slide`).

fields.name: axisOvertravel
fields.doc: Room past the travel of axis `id` before its rail blocks reach the rail ends, in millimetres.

fields.name: orient
fields.doc: Frame whose local +Y points along `up` and local +Z along `along`: perpendicular unit vectors (a parallel pair is refused).

fields.name: place
fields.doc: A fixed root member at its world pose.

fields.name: attach
fields.doc: A member fixed to `parent`, at its world pose with every axis at zero.

fields.name: hang
fields.doc: Adds `component` at `pose` as a child of `parent` without a mate: the caller adds the joint.

fields.name: seat
fields.doc:
Declares seat `name` on member `parent` at `frame`, in that member's own frame: a place the design puts a part on it,
for a part that does not declare its own seats (a rail, a tube). Plates declare theirs (`SeatedPlate`).

fields.name: seatAt
fields.doc: Declares seat `name` on member `parent` at `world`, a frame in assembly coordinates with every axis at zero.

fields.name: mountAt
fields.doc:
Mounts `component` as `id` by its connector `connector` on a seat of `parent` that the design puts where that connector
lies with the component at `pose`: the part sits on its real interface. The seat, `seat-<id>`, carries the mounted
member's id, so members that share one definition (a left and a right column) keep their seats apart.

fields.name: localFrame
fields.doc: `world` (a frame in assembly coordinates) in the frame of something at `pose`: how a part's seat is written in its own coordinates.

fields.name: axes
fields.doc: A frame at (x, y, z) whose local +X and +Z point along `xAxis` and `zAxis` (square to each other); +Y is Z x X.

fields.name: mount
fields.doc:
Mounts `component` as `id` on `parent`'s seat `seat` by the component's own connector `connector`: the member sits
where the seat puts it, its connector's frame on the seat's. Seats belong to the carrying part (or were declared with
`seat`), so a member is never placed first and its carrier's connector invented where it landed.

fields.name: slideOn
fields.doc:
Block `id` slides on rail `rail`: at coordinate zero it sits `at` millimetres along the rail from its start, and a
growing coordinate moves it towards the rail's far end (`sense` 1) or its start (-1). Its pose, the joint's axis and
the axis's travel direction all come from the rail; the axis's overtravel is the room its block has left on the rail
at either end of travel, where the rail's end stops are.

fields.name: slide
fields.signature: (spec:AxisSpec, parent:String, id:String, component:MachineComponent, pose:AssemblyFrame, axis:{x:Float, y:Float, z:Float}, ?additionalBlockPoses:Array<AssemblyFrame>, ?overtravelLimit:Float):Void
fields.doc:
A rail block sliding on its rail (`parent`) along a world axis; `pose` is where it sits at
coordinate zero. The axis's overtravel is the room its block has left on the rail at either end
of travel, where the rail's end stops are. Additional block poses let a
rigid multi-block carriage use the most restrictive block at either end.
An optional overtravelLimit further restricts reserve for bearings or other hardware.

fields.name: slideRail
fields.signature: (spec:AxisSpec, parent:String, id:String, rail:LinearRail, pose:AssemblyFrame, axis:{x:Float, y:Float, z:Float}, blockPoses:Array<AssemblyFrame>):Void
fields.doc: Moving rail on stationary blocks. Travel is checked at both ends for every block.

fields.name: connect
fields.doc:
Connectors meeting at the child's origin with world-aligned axes, so joint axes are world
directions. Names carry the member ids, so members that share geometry can share one
definition holding all of their connectors.

fields.name: driveScrew
fields.signature: (axis:AxisSpec, id:String, motor:String, screw:LeadScrew, pose:AssemblyFrame, along:Array<Float>, flangedNut:Bool, driverForMotor:(String) -> String, ?coupling:ShaftCoupling, ?reducer:MachineComponent):Void
fields.doc:
Motor `motor` turns lead screw `id` (at `pose`, its input end on the shaft tip, pointing
along world direction `along`) through a shaft coupling. Coupling and screw turn together on
a continuous joint `id-turn`, which coupling `id-lead` ties to `axis` by the screw's lead; the
sense follows from the thread and from the direction the axis slides (`slide` comes first).
The coupling is centred on the shaft tip and turns inside the mount's pilot bore.

fields.name: mountNut
fields.doc: Attach the source nut to its carriage once the bracket exists.

fields.name: turnWithBelt
fields.doc: A pulley follows one linear axis, or several for a CoreXY belt.

fields.name: turnCoreXyPulley
fields.signature: (id:String, parent:String, beltId:String, belt:TimingBelt, wrap:BeltWrap, onFrame:Bool, driving:Bool, ?initialX:Float, ?initialY:Float):Void
fields.doc:
A pulley on a CoreXY belt. Its signed contribution from each leader comes from the belt's strand geometry
(`TimingBelt.strands()`) and the side of the belt it wraps (`BeltWrap.side`): the gantry strand, which the
carriage clamps, moves with `x`, and the strand between the frame pulleys moves with `y`. A pulley on the
gantry sees only the carriage moving, so follows `x` alone; a pulley on the frame follows both. `driving` is
the motor's own pulley, which carries torque; every other pulley is an idler.

fields.name: twoPulleyAxis
fields.doc: Build the belt, driving pulley, idler and motor relationship from their actual parts.

fields.name: driveRack
fields.signature: (axis:AxisSpec, id:String, motor:String, pinion:MachineComponent, pose:AssemblyFrame, rackSide:Array<Float>, rackId:String, rack:MachineComponent, ?rackParent:String, driverForMotor:(String) -> String, ?reducer:MachineComponent, ?preload:PreloadedPinionMount):Void
fields.doc:
A moving motor's pinion rolls along a rack fixed to `rackParent`. The pinion sits at `pose` with the axis at
coordinate zero (its axis along the pose's +Z, its face from z = 0 to its face width), and the rack lies on
`rackSide` of it. The rack's pose comes from `rackPlacement`, and the coupling's sense from the pinion rolling
on it as the axis slides (`slide` comes first).

fields.name: rackPlacement
fields.doc:
Where a rack meshes with `pinion` (at `pose` with the axis at zero, see `driveRack`) on its `rackSide` (a direction
from the pinion's axis, square to it and to the axis's travel): the rack's pitch line touches the pinion's pitch
circle, its face is centred on the pinion's, a rack gap faces the pinion tooth nearest the pitch point, and the rack
covers the pitch point over the whole travel with two teeth to spare at each end (or the rack is too short and
this throws). `sense` is the coupling sense that makes the pinion roll on it. Machines size the rack's support from
the pose before calling `driveRack`.

fields.name: screwSense
fields.doc:
The coupling sense of a lead screw pointing along world `along` (its +Z) that drives axis `axisId`: a screw turning by
an angle against its nut moves the nut by its signed lead per turn along +Z (`LeadScrewThread.signedLead`), and
`LeadScrew.relation` gives the turn per unit of travel as alignment * 2 pi / signed lead.

fields.name: addHomeSwitch
fields.signature: (axis:AxisSpec, suffix:String, fixed:String, moving:String, point:Array<Float>, size:Array<Float>, direction:Array<Float>, side:Int, transverse:Array<Float>, ?inductive:Bool, ?shaft:String, ?seed:Int, ?host:{min:Array<Float>, max:Array<Float>}):String
fields.doc:
A home switch for axis `axis` at the end `side` (-1 lower, 1 upper) of its travel: a flag on `moving` (`size` big, its
base centre at `point` with the axis at zero) presses a switch held on `fixed` as the axis comes into that end. The
switch trips a quarter of the axis's overtravel beyond its travel, where its uncertainty still fits before the end
stop; `direction` is the axis's travel direction (along a world axis) and `transverse` the switch's up. The switch is
held by a bracket (`switchBracket`): a plate on its back and, when `fixed` is not right behind it, one leg beside it to
the nearest face of `fixed` (that member's geometry box). An inductive switch senses the flag across its sensing
distance, so its flag is steel; a roller switch
trips at its roller. `seed` numbers switches that share an axis. `host` is the box (assembly coordinates, axes at
zero) of the part of `fixed` the mount is bolted to, when that is not the whole member (one tube of a welded frame).
Returns the switch's member id, `home<suffix>`.

fields.name: switchBracket
fields.doc:
The blocks (assembly coordinates) of a bracket that holds a part whose box is `part`, sensing along `normal` (a world
axis), on a member whose box is `host`: a plate on the part's back (the side away from `normal`) and, unless the plate
already meets the host, one leg to the host. The leg runs straight back from the plate when the host is right behind
it; otherwise it runs beside the part (beyond its face in a sideways axis) to the host's face, so it never passes
through the part. Across the leg's other axes it overlaps the host's face by up to `contact`, a face contact rather
than an edge, while stopping at the face in its own axis, so it never enters the host.

types.name: AxisSpec
types.doc: Travel and initial coordinate of a linear joint, in assembly units.

types.name: BeltAxisMotion
types.doc: One linear leader contributing to a belt pulley's shaft angle.

types.name: BeltPathRecord
types.doc: Physical clamp and pulley centres, in belt path order. The clamp span follows its geometry.

types.name: Carriage
types.doc: Block riding the lead screw. CAD frame: bore centred, spanning z=0..length.

fields.name: railMountY
fields.doc: Carriage-side mounting frame for a profile rail block, when this carriage uses one.

fields.name: componentType
fields.doc: Subclasses must declare their own recipe and saved values.

types.name: ControllerWiring
types.doc: Derives control domains from cabinet terminals, drive inputs and valve coils.

types.name: CylinderRecord
types.doc: A fluid cylinder on a prismatic joint; pressure, force and direction come from installed parts.

types.name: Diagnostics
types.doc: Ordered validation findings; callers can inspect all errors before acting.

types.name: DriveSystem
types.doc:
One level's drives and their feedback: transmissions that set coupling ratios from their parts,
belt paths, motors, pneumatic cylinders, encoders and switch, at-speed and presence sensors.
Resolving them works on the flattened assembly, since a motor's supply or a belt's pulleys may sit
in another level.

fields.name: derive
fields.doc:
Write every transmission's coupling from its parts into `flat.definition`, and the elastic
networks of shared belts. Findings go to `flat.diagnostics`; an unresolved transmission keeps
its stated coupling.

fields.name: apply
fields.doc: Resolve `transmission` and write its coupling; false when the coupling does not exist.

fields.name: write
fields.doc: Write a resolved relation into the coupling and its follower joint's speed limit.

fields.name: driverVoltage
fields.doc: A modelled supply wins over the explicit fallback; an exposed boundary has no voltage of its own.

fields.name: checkMotor
fields.doc:
Check a motor binding against the parts as far as they are wired now. An incomplete module may
be wired by the assembly that includes it; its complete power graph is resolved on export.

fields.name: checkElectricalSources
fields.doc: Check the whole wired source, including simultaneous peak loads and regeneration.

fields.name: compileMotors
fields.doc: Compile every binding anew; connecting a supply after binding must not leave an old curve.

fields.name: checkCylinder
fields.doc: Check a cylinder binding: typed cylinder and valve parts on a prismatic tree joint with no other drive.

fields.name: airPressure
fields.doc: Gauge pressure at a pneumatic consumer.

fields.name: fluidPressure
fields.doc: Gauge pressure at a fluid consumer, traced through its current service wiring to a modelled supply.

types.name: EncoderRecord
types.doc:
An encoder part reading a joint (see `MachineAssembly.addEncoder`), and the motor's actuator it
reads when it is that motor's feedback.

types.name: FlangeBearingAssembly
types.doc:
Flange bearing housing with its bearing pressed in and four mounting screws, composed from
standalone `MachineComponent`s rather than being one itself: `addTo` places the housing at
`pose` and mates the bearing and screws onto it, so the whole block moves together.

The bearing is centred in the housing (its `axis` on the housing's mid-depth `bore`). The
screws pass through the housing from its outer face (z=depth), heads seated there, into the
frame the mounting face (z=0) bolts to: their length is the next ISO 4762 standard length of at
least the housing depth plus 1.5 screw diameters of thread engagement. `addTo` adds a
`bolt<i>Head` connector (the bolt centre on the outer face, +Y along +Z) to the housing
instance for each screw seat. The bearing's own `front`/`axis`/`back` connectors (named
`'<id>-bearing'`) stay reachable for mating a shaft through it.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
`bearingFitted` false leaves the bore empty, as a housing is fastened before a later station presses its
bearing in; the housing stays sized for that bearing.

fields.name: standardScrewLength
fields.doc: Shortest ISO 4762 preferred length at least `minimum` millimetres.

types.name: FlangeTappedPlate
types.doc: Aluminium fixture plate with four independently named taps on the housing's bolt square.

types.name: FlatAssembly
types.doc:
An assembly and all of its subassemblies in one namespace of member paths. Checks, transmissions,
motors, mass and every export work on this view; `MachineAssembly` builds it and drops it on edit.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: Occurrences, connectors, joints and couplings with path ids; derived couplings once `derived`.

fields.name: portExposures
fields.doc: The ports the assembly itself exposes; a subassembly's own exposures are internal here.

fields.name: diagnostics
fields.doc: Findings from working the transmission couplings out from their parts.

fields.name: derived
fields.doc: Whether `DriveSystem.derive` has written the transmissions into `definition`.

fields.name: motorFindings
fields.doc: Nominal receiving interface only. This does not qualify shaft reach or fasteners.

types.name: HzMotionComponent
types.doc:
Purchased-component interfaces from pinned drawings. Existing drawing recipes
stay parametric; the separate supplier recipe enables reviewed motor housings and BF supports.
Detailed CAD does not establish installed clip state or mechanical qualification.

types.name: HzMotionHole
types.doc: Reviewed drawing data, mm/kg. These are interface records, not verified offers.

types.name: InstancePath
types.doc: A slash-separated occurrence path; each segment is a local instance name.

types.name: IntegrityReport
types.doc: What one `AssemblyIntegrity.check` found, and how much it looked at.

types.name: LeaderMove
types.doc: The root leader of a drive, where it rests and the small step the drive check moves it by.

types.name: LinearAxis
types.doc:
Parametric lead-screw axis. The screw rotates through a coupling; a separate prismatic
joint keeps the carriage oriented to the fixed frame. `setTravel` sets the carriage coordinate;
its transmission coupling turns the screw. The default uses two fixed round guide rods passing
through linear bearings carried by the carriage; `forRailProfile()` selects a catalog-backed profile rail
and block closure instead. The nut's flange mounts on the carriage's motor-facing side.

Layout along the screw: coupling, flange bearing A, end margin, carriage travel, end margin,
then flange bearing B. The margin clears the nut protruding from the carriage. Flange bearing
housings, guide rods and the frame rail are fixed roots in the assembly. The `LinearGuideSystem`
keeps the guide bearing catalog row and shaft/seat fit intent with those parts. Their real
mounting structure and screw bearing closure remain outside this kinematic preview.

fields.name: COUPLING_GAP
fields.doc: Axial gap between the coupling's end and flange bearing A's housing.

fields.name: RAIL_GAP
fields.doc: Gap between the rail and the widest part around the screw.

fields.name: guideSystem
fields.doc: Round-rod guide retained for the default axis and for source compatibility.

fields.name: railGuide
fields.doc: Profile-rail guide selected by `forRailProfile`; null for the round-rod default.

fields.name: railGuideOffset
fields.doc: World-z offset of the profile rail's axis connector from the screw input.

fields.name: screwStart
fields.doc: World z of the screw's input end, with the motor at the identity pose.

fields.name: bearingAPosition
fields.doc: Flange bearing centres, measured from the screw's input end.

fields.name: travelMin
fields.doc: Carriage joint limits: bore centre measured from the screw's input end.

types.name: MachineAssembly
types.doc:
A reusable machine assembly: MachineComponents, the subassemblies it includes, and how they are
mated, coupled, driven, wired and itemised. Subassemblies stay whole; records on this level name
members below it by path (`arm/link1`). Checks and exports work on one flattened view, built on
demand from the four parts of a level: `MechanicalAssembly`, `ServiceNetwork`, `DriveSystem` and
`AssemblyInventory`.

types.name: MachineAssemblyCodec
types.doc:
Writes and reads `MachineAssemblyDescription`. Each subassembly becomes an entry of the nested
ProjectKit definition's table, with the facts of its own level beside it. A joint or exposure that
reaches into a subassembly goes through a connector that subassembly exposes, named `~path/connector`.

fields.name: encode
fields.doc: The generated codec, after rejecting every member that has no recipe to rebuild it.

fields.name: rebuildMember
fields.doc: Build one member through its recipe.

types.name: MachineAssemblyDescription
types.doc:
A machine assembly as portable data: the nested ProjectKit definition, with each subassembly a
table entry, and the MachineKit facts of the root and of each subassembly.

types.name: MachineLevelRecord
types.doc:
The MachineKit facts of one assembly level. Every member reference is a path below that level, so
a record may name a member of a subassembly (`arm/link1`).

types.name: MechanicalAssembly
types.doc:
One level's parts and how they are put together: its own members, the subassemblies it includes,
connectors it adds or publishes, and its joints and couplings. A reference to a member is a path
below this level, so a joint may attach a member of a subassembly (`arm/link1`).

fields.name: order
fields.doc: Members and subassemblies by local id, in the order they were added.

fields.name: groundPlaced
fields.doc:
Grounds each component occurrence that no tree joint carries. A placed member stays where its assembly puts it
(the simulation bolts it to the world), so the editor's mates never move it; without the flag the mate solver
grounds only the first root and floats every other placed member.

fields.name: checkStructure
fields.doc: Mate-tree faults: two parents, cycles, and couplings between missing joints.

types.name: MemberRecord
types.doc: A member of one level, by its local name.

types.name: MemberSource
types.doc: Serializable recipe inputs. The constructor IDs are part of the wire schema.

types.name: MotorBrakeRecord
types.doc:
Motor and driver members driving a joint, its actuator given `margin` of the motor's holding
torque (see `MachineAssembly.addMotor`). Voltage and current come from the driver.

types.name: NemaMountPlate
types.doc: NEMA pilot and bolt-clearance plate. Its back at z=0 mates to the motor face.

fields.name: mountScrew
fields.doc: The existing MotorShaftBearings design: 0.5 mm tip clearance and at least 1.3 diameters engagement.

types.name: PartBox
types.doc: An axis-aligned box, in mm.

types.name: PosedParts
types.doc:
Parts of an assembly placed at poses for clearance checks, which pose the same part again and again (against each of
several others, at each position of a sweep).

A component's geometry is built once per `geometryKey` and kept, with its box; each pose is a new part made by moving it, so
the expensive solid construction is not repeated. Pair checks (`overlap`, `volume`, `checkClear`) first compare the posed
boxes (`box`, the kept box carried to the pose) and move geometry only for pairs that may touch: moving a solid copies it
and measuring its tight box afterwards is an optimisation over its surfaces, and most posed pairs are far apart. The kept
shapes are native and belong to this object: close it when the check is done. Poses it returned are the caller's to close
and stay valid after it is closed.

fields.name: APART_MARGIN
fields.doc: Parts whose boxes are further apart than this (mm) are not tested with a boolean.

fields.name: local
fields.doc: `component`'s geometry in its own frame, built on first use and kept by this object (do not close it).

fields.name: posed
fields.doc: `component`'s geometry moved to `pose`: a new owned part.

fields.name: moved
fields.doc: `part` moved to `pose`: a new owned part.

fields.name: box
fields.doc:
A box holding `component` at `pose`, without moving its geometry: the box of its kept geometry carried to the pose. It
contains the box `boxOf` measures on the posed part and is larger when the pose rotates the part, so a pair whose boxes
are `apart` here is apart in fact.

types.name: RbkMotorMount
types.doc:
Pinned RBK assembly geometry, normalized to X across, Y up, Z motor-to-bearing.
Motor face Z=0; base bearing plane Y=0. The flange underhang needs base relief.
Axis frames do not establish shaft seating, bearing preload or load capacity.

fields.name: setSupplierDirectory
fields.doc: Asset location is deployment configuration; saved recipes pin identity, never an absolute path.

fields.name: interfaceMetadata
fields.doc: Defensive evidence copy: nominal drawing dimensions, measured CAD bolt centres and limitations.

fields.name: motorThreadDepth
fields.doc: Drawing value only; null where absent. Not a measured effective thread engagement.

types.name: RobotZoneBox
types.doc: One box of a robot zone: its centre and half extents in millimetres, in the zone connector's frame.

types.name: ScrewAxisComponents
types.doc:
Selected engineering parts, independent of supplier offers.
This template supports the drawing-checked RBK12/SFU16 end stack; it does not
treat all products called BF12 or NEMA23 as interchangeable.

fields.name: blockThreadDepth
fields.doc: The carriage's tapped mounting depth from its table, NaN when the table gives none.

fields.name: motorWasher
fields.doc: Optional ISO7089 M4 washers; the selected motor must clear their 9 mm outside diameter.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (mount:RbkMotorMount, motor:NemaStepper, screw:LeadScrew, nut:LeadScrewNut, support:VallderBf12Support, rail:LinearRail, block:LinearRailBlock, ?motorWasher:Bool):Void

types.name: ScrewAxisCoupling
types.doc:
Existing rigid sleeve generator, 6.35/10 bores, D25 L40. Installed engagement
8.6 mm motor and 11.5 mm screw; 19.9 mm gap. Reference design, no supplier SKU.

types.name: ScrewAxisLayout
types.doc:
Fabrication layout for the supported twin HGR15 / SFU16 / RBK12 interface.
Coordinates are millimetres: X across, Y off the base, Z along travel.
Lengths and spacing vary; cross sections remain an explicitly checked interface family.

types.name: ScrewAxisPart
types.doc: Saveable fabrication for a checked ScrewAxisLayout. Legacy example recipes remain separate.

types.name: Sense
types.doc: Orientation of a transmission relative to its joints.

types.name: ServiceNetwork
types.doc:
One level's service wiring: connections between member ports and the ports it publishes. Tracing
and checks work on the flattened assembly, where a subassembly's connections are prefixed.

fields.name: check
fields.doc: Connection faults, and with `required` every required consumer left without a supply.

fields.name: trace
fields.doc: Follow a service upstream through connections, bridges and a single-input converter.

types.name: Sfu20AxisLayout
types.doc: Drawing-checked SFU20/BK15/BF15/DSG20/HG20 layout, mm. No purchased part is resized.

types.name: Sfu20AxisPart
types.doc: Fabricated base, risers, carriage and motor bracket for a standard purchased SFU20 stack.

types.name: SubassemblyRecord
types.doc: One subassembly: its path from the root, its entry in the mechanical table, and its facts.

types.name: SupportedSfu20Axis

fields.name: installationClearances
fields.doc:
Every component pair, including hardware, except explicitly listed threaded/contact pairs.
Samples include eight shaft phases to expose rotating clamp-head clearance.

types.name: SweepSample
types.doc: One sampled joint state of a sweep: the bodies' motion from rest, the joint values, and the pairs already reported.

types.name: Transmission
types.doc: Parts that define a coupling. The leader is the coordinate motion is planned in.

fields.name: LeadScrew
fields.doc:
The nut rides the leader's slide; the screw turns on the follower. Same follows the screw's
thread handedness: positive slide turns a right-hand screw negatively.

fields.name: GearMesh
fields.doc:
The driver turns on the leader and meshes with the follower's gear. Same is an external mesh,
so the gears turn in opposite directions.

fields.name: RackAndPinion
fields.doc:
The follower's pinion rolls along the leader's rack. Same maps positive rack travel to
positive pinion rotation.

fields.name: TimingBelt
fields.doc:
The driving pulley turns with the belt clamped to the leader. Same maps positive belt
travel to positive pulley rotation.

fields.name: RollerChain
fields.doc:
A roller chain is a separate family from a timing belt. Same maps positive chain travel
to positive sprocket rotation.

fields.name: BeltIdler
fields.doc: An idler follows belt motion and contributes bearing drag, without delivering torque.

fields.name: BeltReduction
fields.doc:
Two pulleys on one belt, named by their coordinate joints. The motor may be on either
pulley; the leader is the planned coordinate, not the source of mechanical power.

types.name: TransmissionRecord
types.doc: Source of a derived coupling; the follower is zero at `leaderZero`.

types.name: TwinRailScrewAxis
types.doc:
Reusable purchased-support twin-rail axis for the checked RBK12/SFU16/HGR15 interface.
Component selection and fabrication layout are explicit inputs; purchasing stays in SourcingPlan.
Unlike the generic LinearAxis rod/rail envelope, this template includes the actual support stack
and installation hardware. The supplier CAD's 0.5 mm stack discrepancy is retained.

fields.name: installationClearances
fields.doc:
Nominal solid intersections at start, midpoint and end. Thread penetration is intentional;
only installation pairs which must clear are tested. This is not a load/preload qualification.

types.name: TwoPulleyAxis
types.doc: A belt drive's mechanical layout. The machine supplies its idler mounting hardware.

types.name: Catalog
types.doc: Designation-keyed table of standard sizes, kept separate from geometry code.

types.name: CatalogIndex
types.doc: Read-only designation and provenance index shared by editable catalog inputs.

types.name: CatalogMetadata
types.doc: Provenance and limits of one catalog entry. A null edition means it has not been verified.

types.name: Conformance
types.doc: Scope of the generated geometry and interfaces.

types.name: DimensionKind
types.doc: How the listed dimensions relate to the cited source.

types.name: FilteredCatalogIndex
types.doc: Designation subset of an existing catalog, retaining its provenance metadata.

types.name: PinnedCad
types.doc: Reviewed supplier CAD files pinned by content: geometry loads only a file whose SHA-256 matches its review.

fields.name: sha256
fields.doc: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the file at `path`.

fields.name: require
fields.doc: `path`, once it exists and matches `digest`; `prepare` says how to fetch it.

types.name: AssumedCatalogComponent
types.doc:
Unverified catalogue-class layout part. Ratings and envelopes are assumptions,
never vendor data. Subclasses supply a saved recipe and meaningful interfaces.

types.name: Bom
types.doc: Aggregates bill-of-materials lines by part number.

fields.name: lines
fields.doc: Lines in first-added order.

types.name: CollisionHullFacet
types.doc: Authored convex pieces in the component's local CAD frame, preserving routed gaps.

fields.name: aroundCircularOpenings
fields.doc: Rectangular collision proxy with circumscribed square cutouts around round openings.

fields.name: prism
fields.doc: A bounded convex profile, in CAD millimetres; no union hull fills a neighbouring gap.

fields.name: cylinder
fields.doc: Inscribed cylinder proxy, retaining the exact axial limits and cardinal radii.

fields.name: fromExtrusion
fields.doc: Extrude an authored constant section from its actual top cap, retaining every hole.

types.name: ComponentClassification
types.doc:
How MachineKit's built-in recipes are filed for catalogues and part pickers: a category within each package
(the id's second segment) and a kind. Categories are listed here in display order. A recipe added to
`MachineKitComponents` without a row here fails RecipeContractTests.

types.name: ComponentDetail
types.doc: Geometry fidelity requested from a component generator.

fields.name: Envelope
fields.doc: Outer envelope for clearance and packaging; moving parts cover their full travel.

fields.name: Preview
fields.doc: Recognizable exterior features with simplified internals.

types.name: ComponentDisplayMesh
types.doc: Optional display tessellation; CAD, collision geometry and physical properties remain explicit.

types.name: ComponentEnvelopes
types.doc:
Simple envelope geometry only; engineering facts belong to optional facets.
Geometry methods return a new owned Part for the caller to close.

types.name: ComponentFacet
types.doc:
A typed fact a part states about itself, such as a suction contact or a welding supply. Each kind
is its own class in the package of its domain, so a new domain adds a class rather than changing
the component core; look one up with that class's `of`.

fields.name: check
fields.doc: Throws when `component` lacks a port or connector this facet names, or a value is out of range.

fields.name: describe
fields.doc: The facet and its values in words, for diagnostics and comparisons.

types.name: ComponentFamily
types.doc:
One interface contract, one serializable recipe, explicit manufacturing alternatives.
The recipe must carry the variant in its normal values/BOM key. Geometry-level
compliance with interfaceId is established by the family's own checks.

types.name: ComponentKind
types.doc: What a component recipe stands for, for catalogues and part pickers.

fields.name: Generic
fields.doc: A reusable parametric recipe, sized by its inputs or a standard catalogue.

fields.name: Supplier
fields.doc: A named supplier's product, with that supplier's data.

fields.name: Reference
fields.doc: A drawing, study or reference envelope: geometry to check against, not a part to buy or make.

fields.name: MachinePart
fields.doc: A part designed for one machine (an example's frame, guard or bracket).

types.name: ComponentParameter
types.doc: Description and validation of one editable generator input.

types.name: ComponentParameterType
types.doc: Supported editable inputs for a single machine part.

types.name: ComponentRecipeSupport
types.doc: Shared parameter constructors and parsed enum inputs for component recipes.

fields.name: resolve
fields.doc:
Resolve direct-constructor inputs using the same schema as recipe creation.
Material is an optional reserved override for constructors; ComponentType already declares it.

fields.name: quantity
fields.doc: A quantity whose engineering unit travels with its recipe schema.

fields.name: interfaceParameters
fields.doc: Inputs describing a port's mating interface, under one name prefix.

types.name: ComponentRegistry
types.doc: Component recipes by stable id; loading a saved assembly rebuilds its members through one.

fields.name: classify
fields.doc:
Files a registered type under a category (a heading within its package, such as "Linear guides") and a kind,
for catalogues and part pickers. MachineKit's built-ins are all classified (`ComponentClassification`).

fields.name: categoryNames
fields.doc: Every category, in the order types were first filed under it (the display order).

fields.name: category
fields.doc: The type's category, or null when it has not been classified.

fields.name: all
fields.doc: Registered types in registration order.

types.name: ComponentType
types.doc: Stable recipe for one kind of single part.

fields.name: materialEditable
fields.doc: False when a typed mechanical input already determines the material.

fields.name: knownMass
fields.doc:
Mass properties already computed for a component of this type, by its `MachineComponent.geometryKey(Preview)`. They come
from cutting and integrating real solids, and each machine compile builds new component instances, so a per-instance
cache never hit across compiles. `MassProperties` never changes, so one value can be shared by every such component.

fields.name: bomKey
fields.doc: BOM identity omits recipe inputs that only place or route a physical part.

types.name: ComponentValue
types.doc: Stored input value; its variant must match the parameter type.

types.name: ComponentValues
types.doc: Named typed values for one component recipe.

types.name: ComponentView
types.doc:
How a component is best looked at on its own (catalogue thumbnails, part previews): which of its local
directions points up on screen, and which faces the viewer's side. A component declares one through
`MachineComponent.presentationView` when its shape alone does not say; otherwise `derive` chooses from its
bounds. Directions are unit vectors in the component's CAD frame and must be perpendicular.

fields.name: up
fields.doc: Shown pointing up.

fields.name: front
fields.doc: Shown facing the viewer's side; the camera then looks at the part from a little to one side and above.

fields.name: upright
fields.doc: Standing as modelled: +Z up, -Y towards the viewer.

fields.name: lengthAlongZ
fields.doc:
Lying down for a part that runs along its local +Z with its working face towards +Y (rails, racks, screws,
profiles, keys): +Y up and the length running across the view.

fields.name: derive
fields.doc: The view for a part with these CAD bounds: lying down when it is much longer along Z than across, else upright.

types.name: Connector
types.doc: A named frame in the component's CAD coordinates. Joints act along its +Y axis.

types.name: ConnectorRole
types.doc: Descriptive tag for a connector frame; mating always uses the frame itself.

fields.name: Axis
fields.doc: Rotation or symmetry axis along the frame's +Y.

fields.name: Face
fields.doc: Planar contact face whose outward normal is the frame's +Y.

fields.name: Mount
fields.doc: Mounting interface, such as a flange face or bolt position.

fields.name: Shaft
fields.doc: End of a drive shaft that receives a coupling, pulley, or gear.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.doc: Contact datum on a gear or rack's theoretical pitch surface.

types.name: CouplingFacet
types.doc: A coupling half: it mates at `connector` with any half whose `key` is the same.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: The facet of this kind on `component`, or null.

types.name: Dimension
types.doc: Formatting for dimensions embedded in designations and part numbers.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: Decimal text for `value` rounded to 0.001 mm.

types.name: EffectiveDensities
types.doc:
Assumed effective densities (kg/m³) of purchased parts whose envelope is a housing around air, electronics and
terminals: datasheet mass over envelope volume for reference products of the class (2026-10-21). They replace
the mass of a solid block of the housing material, which overstates such parts five to ten times. A catalogue
row's datasheet mass, where one is known, overrides them (`MachineComponent.declareMass`).

types.name: EngineeringMetadata
types.doc: Optional engineering provenance, independent of shape and recipe storage.

fields.name: assumedCatalog
fields.doc: An unverified reference row carries its source instead of implying catalogue verification.

types.name: ExtrusionCollision
types.doc:
Convex pieces for a union of constant-section machined plates. Round edges use 0.05 mm / 0.5 rad collision tessellation. Every hole
is taken from the actual cap mesh, not replaced by the union's convex hull.

types.name: GeometryFidelity
types.doc: How faithfully a component's preview geometry represents the real part.

fields.name: Envelope
fields.doc: The preview is a placeholder of the part's size: one primitive solid such as a box, cylinder or ring.

fields.name: Nominal
fields.doc: Recognisable features in generic proportions.

fields.name: Datasheet
fields.doc: Key dimensions from a cited standard or datasheet.

fields.name: Supplier
fields.doc: The supplier's own CAD.

types.name: IncludedInPurchase
types.doc: A physical subpart carried by the separately listed purchase, rather than ordered on its own.

types.name: MachineComponent
types.doc:
Geometry generator, named connector frames, and a BOM line for one machine part.
`geometry()` returns a new owned Part in the component's CAD frame; the caller closes it.

fields.name: materialId
fields.doc: Physical material changes go through setMaterial, so mechanically typed parts can enforce their class.

fields.name: codeOnly
fields.doc: True when this component was built from explicit, non-catalog specifications.

fields.name: instanceId
fields.doc: Tells this component from every other, including ones built from the same recipe.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: Null for code-only parts and assemblies outside the v1 recipe registry.

fields.name: facets
fields.doc: The typed facts this part states about itself; look one kind up with its class's `of`.

fields.name: motorDrive
fields.doc: Typed electrical endpoints, absent on unrelated components.

fields.name: simulationContact
fields.doc: Explicit contact assumptions for this part's generated simulation hull.

fields.name: cylinderSpec
fields.doc: Typed fluid model when this component is a cylinder.

fields.name: valveSpec
fields.doc: Typed fluid model when this component is a directional valve.

fields.name: pressureSource
fields.doc: Typed pressure data when this component supplies a fluid service.

fields.name: lockManufacturingMaterial
fields.doc: Factories lock a process-specific material without changing ordinary component recipes.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc:
How this part is best looked at on its own, when its shape alone does not say (see `ComponentView.derive`);
null leaves the choice to its bounds.

fields.name: geometryKey
fields.doc:
Names the geometry `geometry(detail)` builds, for a cache of it: the same for every component made from the same recipe
inputs and material, which build the same shape, and for a component without a recipe (nothing says which components are
alike) its own.

fields.name: geometryFidelity
fields.doc:
How faithful the preview is. Derived where the geometry shows it: a preview that is one primitive solid (six
faces or fewer: a box, a cylinder, a ring or a tube) is a placeholder of the part's size, `Envelope`; any other
is `Nominal`. Parts dimensioned from a cited standard or datasheet declare `Datasheet`, imports of supplier CAD
`Supplier`.

types.name: MachineIo
types.doc: Required controller channels. Hardwired safety contacts are separate component ports.

types.name: MachineKitComponents
types.doc: MachineKit's built-in component recipes, registered package by package.

fields.name: standard
fields.doc: A new registry holding only the built-in recipes.

fields.name: defaultRegistry
fields.doc:
The registry saved assemblies load through unless the caller passes one: the built-ins plus
whatever an application registers into it before loading.

types.name: ManufacturingVariant
types.doc: Declared manufacturing intent, not a certificate of process or load capability.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (id:String, process:String, material:String, status:String, hardware:Array<{partNumber:String, quantity:Int, description:String, material:String}>, pendingChecks:Array<String>):Void

types.name: MassProperties
types.doc: Mass in kg, centre in mm, and centroidal inertia in kg mm² in the component frame.

types.name: MassSource
types.doc: Origin of a component's mass and centre of mass estimate.

fields.name: EffectiveDensity
fields.doc:
A purchased part's mass: its envelope's volume at an assumed effective density (kg/m³) for its product class
(`EffectiveDensities`), not its drawn housing. An authored value, like `Declared`.

fields.name: Modelled
fields.doc:
Computed from a simplified solid that stands in for the part's mass (`MachineComponent.massGeometry`), at its
material's density, so drawing detail does not move it. An authored model, like `Declared`.

types.name: NoGeometry
types.doc: Raised by components that do not define a shape for mass estimation.

types.name: PortBridge
types.doc: Directed passage through a component, from its inlet to outlet.

fields.name: Coupling
fields.doc: Integrated changer feed-through; the key and channel must match across halves.

types.name: PortInterfaces
types.doc:
Service-port mating rules. Thread designations with -M/-F include sex;
designations without a suffix match exactly.

fields.name: Gas
fields.doc: Shielding gas, which does not mix with compressed air.

fields.name: Wire
fields.doc: Consumable welding wire, fed from a spool through a liner.

fields.name: Hydraulic
fields.doc: Hydraulic oil service, distinct from compressed air.

fields.name: ScrewFeed
fields.doc: Oriented separated screws through a commissioned delivery tube.

types.name: Solids
types.doc: MachineKit helpers that consume parts, plus its joint-axis convention.

fields.name: building
fields.doc:
Build a result while tracking temporary parts. If the callback throws, every still-open
part in `parts` is closed before the original error is rethrown. Successful callbacks keep
the same consuming semantics as `union` and `cut`.

fields.name: named
fields.doc:
`part` with its faces, edges and vertices named under `tag` (`body`, `shaft`, `bolt2`), closing `part`. Name the
bodies of a recipe whose faces users may pick, so a mate on them follows the face as parameters change
(cadkit/plans/TOPOLOGICAL_NAMING.md). Use names that mean the same body for every parameter value, never an index
that shifts when an optional body comes or goes.

fields.name: union
fields.doc: Fuse all parts and close each input.

fields.name: cut
fields.doc: Subtract all tools and close the base and tools.

fields.name: axial
fields.doc: Frame at a point whose +Y joint axis points along CAD +Z.

types.name: SourcingPlan
types.doc: Optional sourcing overlay. Engineering BOM identity and aggregation never depend on supplier.

fields.name: select
fields.doc: Explicit preference, including a provisional candidate; export still reports review_required.

types.name: SupplierCadComponent
types.doc:
Local, hash-pinned supplier geometry. Has no inferred mounting connectors or mechanical ratings.
Prefer an existing parametric recipe when one describes the required part.
Caller owns this import and must close it; each geometry() result is independently owned.

types.name: SupplierOffer
types.doc:
One sourcing option for an engineering BOM part. Prices are snapshot minor units.
A nominal geometric match must retain compatibilityVerified=false until reviewed.

types.name: SupplierRecipeLibrary
types.doc:
Supplier bindings instantiate existing recipes; this class contains no geometry code.
Bound size/material inputs cannot be overridden. Required cut-length inputs remain explicit.

types.name: ToolSpec
types.doc: Editable, typed inputs for a named cutting tool produced by a component.

types.name: CncController
types.doc: CNC cabinet with drive references, digital inputs, general outputs and valve coils.

types.name: ControlCabinet
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class control cabinet with DIN rows and derived I/O. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: forParts
fields.doc: Build-time count from actual components; channels remain named for SR17 wiring.

types.name: ControlComponents
types.doc: The control package's component recipes.

types.name: ControllerCabinet
types.doc: A physical cabinet with individually wired drive and digital I/O terminals.

types.name: DigitalSensor
types.doc: A field switch, presence head or safety area scanner with one digital output terminal.

types.name: EmergencyStopButton
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class latching emergency stop with two NC contacts. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

types.name: RobotController
types.doc: Robot cabinet with one drive reference per axis and separately wired digital I/O.

types.name: SafetyRelay
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class dual-channel safety relay with delayed contacts. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

types.name: ThermistorInput
types.doc:
Controller ADC front end: NTC to ground, pull-up to an assumed ideal reference.
The envelope is authored, not a verified board layout; ADC quantization and pin
assignments belong to a concrete controller. All electrical values are explicit.

fields.name: voltage
fields.doc: Divider voltage, including a short (zero ohms) and open circuit (positive infinity).

types.name: ERobDriveInterface
types.doc: SI-unit boundary; a future EtherCAT backend owns ESI/PDO scaling and CiA402 transitions.

types.name: ERobDriveStub
types.doc: Deterministic command-loop stub. Never opens a NIC or enables a physical brake/drive.

types.name: AssemblyDesignChecks
types.doc:
No machine names, dimensions or member IDs: evaluates component facets and
portable assembly requirements. Assembly phases explicitly name installed
parts; service requirements see the entire containing machine by default.

types.name: BlindThreadInterface
types.doc: +Z enters the material from the drilling face. Drill depth includes the point envelope.

types.name: DesignChecks
types.doc:
Geometric/process limits supplied by the designer, in mm; not strength qualification.
Callers own every shape. Access envelopes must include approach/withdrawal, not only the seated tool.

fields.name: blindFastener
fields.signature: (out:Diagnostics, subject:String, length:Float, grip:Float, threadDepth:Float, cylindricalDrillDepth:Float, drillTip:Float, thickness:Float, minEngagement:Float, minTipGap:Float, minBack:Float, ?reliefStart:Float):Void

fields.name: coaxial
fields.doc: Axes may point in opposite directions; transverse position must agree.

fields.name: material
fields.doc:
Required ligament ring/shell must be wholly contained in the actual cut solid.
This catches nearby holes and pockets as well as the outer boundary.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: Include clearance in the envelope itself. No exemptions for touching a tool shaft.

types.name: DesignInterfaces
types.doc:
Optional component facet. Recipes regenerate these facts; solids are never
stored in metadata. The same hole descriptions can generate machining tools.

types.name: DesignObstacles
types.doc:
InstalledMembers describes a bench/assembly phase. WholeAssembly includes
surrounding parts added by the containing machine, without hardcoded lists.

fields.name: InterfaceAlignment
fields.doc:
id identifies this assembly occurrence; relationship.id identifies the
design relationship referenced by the source interfaces, across occurrences.

fields.name: Coaxial
fields.doc: Nominal hole/connector axes; physical metrology is a separate requirement.

types.name: DesignRequirements
types.doc: Copies portable data and remaps every reference when nesting an assembly.

types.name: DesignVolume
types.doc: Portable shapes in the declared interface frame; lengths in mm.

types.name: FoundationJointDesignChecks
types.doc: Native source resolution followed by the same nominal checks as tooling.

types.name: FoundationJointSourceSupport
types.doc: Copy source components, never infer hole patterns or support dimensions.

types.name: InterfaceSourceSupport
types.doc: One reference resolver for design diagnostics and detached tooling snapshots.

types.name: ThreadedHoleChoice
types.doc: Nominal thread paired with its declared machining and clearance sizes.

types.name: ThreadedHolePolicy
types.doc: Design minima, independent of anchorage or coupon evidence. Distances are mm.

fields.name: STEEL_ENGAGEMENT_DIAMETERS
fields.doc:
VDI 2230 Part 1 theoretical 1.3D for Rm >500 MPa / class 8.8,
conservatively using that strength band for C45 bright Rm >=580 MPa.
Bossard, Length of engaged thread, 01-2025, bracketed VDI values:
https://assets.eu.ctfassets.net/0vp0u5uh75zd/3wPlDC2XQOYT3XOdwCk6lz/9a9282ffd29746a7a7f6b0149509f1cf/052_Length_engaged_thread_Fastening_EN_01_2025.pdf
Effective full-thread overlap excludes runout and chamfer.

fields.name: TAP_RUNOUT_PITCHES
fields.doc:
In-house machining allowance: two pitches for a bottoming tap runout.
Usable full thread ends before this zone; drill depth includes it.

fields.name: TIP_GAP_PITCHES
fields.doc: In-house: one pitch of free usable thread beyond the screw tip.

fields.name: BACK_WALL_DIAMETERS
fields.doc: In-house: a quarter diameter of intact steel closes the resin path.

fields.name: RADIAL_WALL_DIAMETERS
fields.doc:
In-house: one diameter of radial steel limits edge breakout and dilation;
this geometric rule does not establish anchorage capacity in the casting.

fields.name: CLEARANCE_DIAMETERS
fields.doc: In-house minimum separation between machined features; not bolt clearance.

fields.name: clearance
fields.doc: Unthreaded bores carry only applicable geometric rules.

types.name: MachineAssemblyDocuments
types.doc: Stores mechanical data through CadKit and MachineKit facts beside it.

fields.name: describeAssembly
fields.doc: The document's assembly as data, with members and port connections read from the document.

types.name: MachineDocumentKind
types.doc: What kind of MachineKit assembly a document holds, with the data its kind adds.

types.name: MachineDocumentRecord
types.doc:
The MachineKit side of an assembly document. Members and port connections are left out of the
stored copy: the document's instances and relationships hold them, so editing those edits the assembly.

types.name: MachineKitDocumentAssembly
types.doc: Adds a document instance and its named connector outputs to a kinematics assembly.

types.name: MachineKitDocuments
types.doc: Definition construction and BOM extraction for MachineKit document instances.

fields.name: placement
fields.doc: Convert the kinematics frame convention to a CadKit local placement.

types.name: MachineKitRecipes
types.doc: CadKit evaluator registration for editable MachineKit single-part recipes.

fields.name: forget
fields.doc: Release cached recipe objects owned by a document that is being closed.

fields.name: reconcile
fields.doc: Merge explicit saved edits onto freshly generated recipe definitions.

fields.name: reconcileDocument
fields.doc: Reconcile in place when the caller already owns a fresh generated document.

types.name: EnclosureCutPanel
types.doc: One through opening in a panel blank: rectangular interface or round extraction port.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (width:Float, height:Float, construction:String, ow:Float, oh:Float, ox:Float, oz:Float, ?diameter:Float):Void

fields.name: facets
fields.doc: Exact rectangular opening proxy; a round port uses its circumscribed square, matching other plate proxies.

types.name: EnclosureFrame
types.doc: Twelve cut 40-series members. Dimensions describe the clear infill opening.

types.name: EnclosureLayout
types.doc: A front-loading shell fitted to declared swept bounds; all dimensions in machine-frame mm.

types.name: EnclosurePanel
types.doc: Rectangular panel: width along X, layer stack along Y, height from Z=0.

types.name: EnclosureRules
types.doc: Catalogue validation reports unknown qualifications as unresolved, never as passing protection.

types.name: GeneratedEnclosure
types.doc: Shell geometry and declared fabrication interfaces. Qualified seals/retention are separate hardware work.

types.name: LaminatedPanel
types.doc: A layer stack with planning mass, explicit provenance and no inferred protective properties.

fields.name: bomProperties
fields.doc: Detailed fabrication/BOM payload; no qualification is promoted from a material name.

types.name: OpposedSlidingDoor
types.doc: Captured roller suspension with lower anti-sway shoes. Drive coupling is ideal; actuator hardware is not modeled.

types.name: PanelCatalogue
types.doc: Initial planning constructions. Thicknesses/densities are assumed; qualification is unfilled.

types.name: PanelQualifications
types.doc: Unknown qualification stays null; nominal material names never establish a rating.

types.name: SlidingDoor
types.doc: Geometric guide and leaf with a real prismatic joint. Closed/open coordinate switches are exported with the assembly.

types.name: TrayClamp
types.doc: Removable stepped toe clamp. Local +X points over the panel; M6 clearance bore is explicit.

types.name: TraySeat
types.doc: Preliminary removable laminate tray stack, millimetres. Gasket/material qualification is separate.

types.name: CylinderControlSpec
types.doc: Cylinder flow law; setup owns the phase profile of a hydraulic binding.

types.name: CylinderPhaseRecord
types.doc: Authored hydraulic flow setup. Stroke and pressure are rebuilt from installed parts.

types.name: CylinderPhaseSpeeds
types.doc: Flow-limited cylinder speeds in mm/s. The change point is extension from home in mm.

fields.name: extensionSpeed
fields.doc: Select the working speed at the change point, including finite end-stop overtravel.

fields.name: extensionTime
fields.doc: Ideal no-load extension time, split at the physical phase-change position.

types.name: CylinderSpec
types.doc: Typed mechanical and force data shared by fluid-powered cylinder components.

types.name: PressureSource
types.doc: A part that states gauge pressure in Pa at a fluid supply port.

types.name: ValveControlSpec
types.doc: Directional spool behaviour exposed by a fluid valve component.

types.name: ValveSpec
types.doc: Typed spool behavior exposed by a directional valve component.

types.name: FrontGuideLayout
types.doc: Front-face four-block X carriage with fixed Z blocks and moving Z rails.

types.name: Gantry
types.doc: Three translational axes assembled from real guides, drives and a standard robot tool flange.

types.name: GantryBeltClamp
types.doc: Belt jaw with a through slot around the belt's actual width and band thickness.

types.name: GantryBoredBracket
types.doc: Connected bracket sections with a bored mounting interface.

types.name: GantryCableChain
types.doc:
Initial routed chain body. The machine owns the axis coordinate and asks
the source chain for posed geometry when updating its preview.

types.name: GantryDrive
types.doc: Mechanical drive choice: ratios are derived from these physical parts.

types.name: GantryExtrusion
types.doc: Cut extrusion, centred in its cross-section and extending along local +Z.

types.name: GantryHead
types.doc: Optional rotary head; the translational assembly exposes the flange without one.

types.name: GantryIdlerPin
types.doc: Stationary journal supporting a belt idler's bore.

types.name: GantryMotor
types.doc: Motor selection is explicit; a braked motor exposes its physical brake for commissioning.

types.name: GantryMotorSupport
types.doc: Frame/carriage bridge with clearance for the actual motor shaft or pinion.

types.name: GantryNutMount
types.doc: Mounting plate seated against the nut flange; bore and bolt holes come from the nut.

types.name: GantryPlate
types.doc: Mounting plate, centred in X/Y with its bottom at Z=0.

types.name: GantrySection
types.doc: Cross-section used by layout and by the actual cut member.

types.name: GantrySpec
types.doc: Travel is in millimetres. Frame and guide dimensions describe parts, not virtual joints.

fields.name: frontExtension
fields.doc: Extra frame length ahead of Y travel, clearing an overhanging tool's vertical sweep.

fields.name: sideExtension
fields.doc: Extra space on each X side between the tool travel and the Y frame guides.

fields.name: frameLift
fields.doc: Extra frame elevation above the default work envelope, in millimetres.

fields.name: toolReach
fields.doc: Requested forward flange reach, in millimetres; enlarged as needed to clear the Z column.

fields.name: racking
fields.doc: Allowed side-to-side displacement; a stated design assumption until measured.

fields.name: assumedFields
fields.doc: Provenance for the authored machine layout and electrical settings.

types.name: GantryStiffenedPlate
types.doc:
Built-up Z plate with two closed side stiffeners; rail mounting face stays flat.
Weld/heat-treatment and final machining remain fabrication qualification inputs.

types.name: GantrySwitchTrigger
types.doc: Side tab and front bridge around a column wider than its Z carriage.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (width:Float, depth:Float, height:Float, bridgeWidth:Float, bridgeDepth:Float, bridgeX:Float, bridgeY:Float):Void

types.name: LinearTrack
types.doc:
Floor-mounted external axis. Dimensions and cable-chain clearance are design assumptions,
while the rack ratio and drive envelope come from its physical parts. Coordinates are mm.

fields.name: cableChainRoom
fields.doc: Unoccupied longitudinal strip beside the carriage for the moving service chain.

fields.name: includeArm
fields.doc: Preserve the arm's level and its drives; only its floor interface is mated here.

types.name: RotaryHead
types.doc:
Servo/gearhead mechanics in a local frame with +Z toward the tool.
Drivers and their power wiring belong to the carrying machine's fixed cabinet.
Dimensions, cable allowances and generic drive ratings are stated design assumptions.

fields.name: driverPhaseCurrent
fields.doc: Driver phase current and brake-resistor demand derived from the installed motor curve.

fields.name: radialEnvelopeMm
fields.doc: Conservative radial clearance for every permitted C/A pose, in millimetres.

fields.name: axialEnvelopeMm
fields.doc: Furthest extent toward the tool over permitted poses, in millimetres.

fields.name: bindDrives
fields.doc: Attach the head's motors to cabinet drivers already wired in the carrying assembly.

types.name: RotaryHeadJoint
types.doc: A head's travel is the intersection of its cable allowance and mechanical stop.

types.name: ExpandingMandrel
types.doc: Hydraulic expanding mandrel. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: FlexsplineCupBlank
types.doc:
One-piece cup blank, open/toothed end at Z=0, closed end above it.
Tooth band and bore use the existing work datum; dimensions are assumed.

types.name: FloatingRadialBearing
types.doc:
Assumed precision needle/roller radial support. No flanges or axial locating
stiffness: the inner race slides +/- axialFloat on the arbor journal.

types.name: FoundationLayout
types.doc: Machine design intent. Exterior openings are authored here, never inferred.

fields.name: TRAY_SOCKET_OUTSIDE_DIAMETER
fields.doc: Unverified exterior study choices; published bore/thread dimensions live in the catalogue variant.

fields.name: driveSupports
fields.doc: Casting-local bounds for the cap, twin webs and bearing cross-ribs.

types.name: Hob
types.doc:
Physical tool envelope, generated from the same rack/HobDesign as the rake cutter.
The optional detailed B-rep uses its rake sections, with explicit assumed relief.

fields.name: fromDesign
fields.doc: Captures the supplied design and enough generating geometry for an exact recipe rebuild.

types.name: HobArbor
types.doc: Hob arbor, assumed taper-and-face interface. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: HobMesh
types.doc:
Display tessellation of the same fused solid used for CAD export.
No independent tooth, core or end-cap construction lives in the renderer.

fields.name: fromShape
fields.doc:
Keep CAD face normals at sharp edges. Coincident boundary positions are
checked geometrically by the mesh tests; normal seams need separate vertices.

types.name: HobSolid
types.doc:
Detailed B-rep from the generating cutter, not an ornamental thread texture.
One comb-shaped land is lofted, then repeated by the exact gash screw transform.

types.name: HobSpindle
types.doc:
Direct B spindle, an assumed 1.5 kW at 4000 rpm / 8000 rpm maximum reference.
Assumed taper/face cartridge; bearing preload and thread detail require specification.

types.name: HobSpindlePart
types.doc:
Dedicated cartridge parts. Dimensions and fits are assumed design values in mm,
not catalogue interfaces. Coordinates share the housing datum.

types.name: HobberBracket
types.doc: Assumed steel carriage/support envelope; structural adequacy awaits Phase D.

types.name: HobberSaddle
types.doc:
Separate designed weldments, with machined mounting datums. Dimensions are mm.
Strength, weld distortion and modal stiffness remain assumed pending Phase D.

types.name: HobberXLayout
types.doc:
Reviewed design dimensions, regenerated/verified by HobberLoadingSizing.
Loading retracts are rounded up from exact-solid corridor analysis, not
inferred from part diameter alone. Changing the head/gripper requires that
acceptance again; the mechanical envelope follows these dimensions.

types.name: HobberZLayout
types.doc:
Central vertical drive datums, mm in the work frame at X=Z=0.
Fixed bearing/motor above the nut; the loaded screw segment works in tension.

types.name: MandrelRadialSupport
types.doc:
Assumed small-displacement n=2 support estimate, N/mm. A simply supported
sleeve mode w=d*cos(pi*z/L)*cos(2 theta) models end rings at +/-L/2.
Bending energy of an isotropic cylindrical shell gives the stated modal k.
Contact is a distributed tangent foundation in series with the sleeve.
Oil resists uniform volume change, but contributes zero to n=2 at first order.
End restraint, surface conformity and contact tangent require calibration.

types.name: MandrelSleeve
types.doc: Separate replaceable sleeve envelope; pressure deformation is NOT solved.

types.name: MineralCastBed
types.doc: Hobber layout on the shared typed foundation model.

types.name: MineralCastColumn
types.doc: Hobber layout on the shared typed foundation model.

types.name: OutboardSupport
types.doc: Hob outboard support housing. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: RotaryClamp
types.doc: Static rotary clamp. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: RotaryTable
types.doc: C-axis package. Joint units rad/rad/s/N m. The clamp is hardware, not active motion coupling.

types.name: SpindleHousing
types.doc: Hob spindle housing. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: SwivelHead
types.doc:
Compact assumed direct-drive swivel: motor inside the crossed-roller ring,
outer clamp in the same axial bay. Procurement and thermal ratings remain assumed.

types.name: SwivelHousing
types.doc: Swivel-head housing. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: TableHousing
types.doc: Rotary table housing. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: TablePlaten
types.doc: Rotary table platen. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: Bt30Cartridge
types.doc:
BT30 packaging study. Ø90 body and Ø125 flange follow the DAIYA BT30SP
envelope; axial interfaces, bearing/shaft internals and mounting holes are
explicit project assumptions, not a supplier interchangeable cartridge.

types.name: Bt30SpindleMotor
types.doc:
Assumed compact 2.2 kW / 8000 rpm motor, including its mounting flange.
This is not the much larger motor in the Automation Technology kit.

fields.name: axialEnvelope
fields.doc: Continuous axial envelope, retaining the narrower body above its flange.

fields.name: massGeometry
fields.doc: Mass of the base motor's body with this flange and pilot, as before the body was drawn in detail.

types.name: Er20Holder
types.doc:
ER20 collet nut and holder around the protruding tool shank, with a 6 mm tool bore.
Origin at the gauge line on the collet nut bottom; the holder extends along +Z.

types.name: FlatEndMill
types.doc:
Visible flat cutter envelope, origin at tool tip. The buried shank is not
represented; stickout is measured from the collet's front face.

types.name: MillBallNutBracket
types.doc: SFU1605 flange bracket, shaft +Z, up +Y. Optional top foot attaches under a table.

types.name: MillBeltMotorPlate
types.doc:
X return-drive motor plate, across X, shaft along Y, bottom Z=0.
Fits a machined saddle recess and the catalog 60 mm Leadshine flange.

types.name: MillBeltSpindle
types.doc: BT30 cartridge driven by a timing belt from a servo beside it (`MillSpindleHead`).

fields.name: HEAD_HEIGHT
fields.doc: Compact VMC head block: clamps the cartridge and carries the motor carrier feet.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `drive` defaults to the installed Leadshine selection for the layout's head height.

types.name: MillCapacityLayout
types.doc:
Packaging study derived from working travel, not a scaled production design.
Guide dimensions come from the pinned local HG25 catalog. Loads, drive sizing,
spindle power and structural performance remain separate engineering decisions.

fields.name: zLayout
fields.doc: Z zero is the top stop: the tool-change position when one is reserved, else the top of the working stroke.

types.name: MillCasting
types.doc:
Machined cast-iron bodies with rail seats, screw clearances and mounting holes.
Dimensions describe this example's designed bodies, rather than a vendor catalogue.

types.name: MillCastingDetails
types.doc: Explicit mill casting intent, in mm; no Boolean extension margins.

fields.name: anchorRule
fields.doc:
Source design rule, shared by all base and column inserts. A minimum
pair resists rotation; long seats add stations at four short-face widths.
Geometric minima do not establish compound-specific anchor capacity.

fields.name: levelingFoot
fields.doc: Nominal complete foot in its floor frame; the assembly mates its 90 mm datum to the seat.

fields.name: columnAnchorThickness
fields.doc:
30 mm stock accommodates the selected M12 service screw, full thread,
bottoming-tap runout, tip gap and intact policy back wall.

fields.name: railHoleBudget
fields.doc: RM0 accuracy allocations are user inputs, not inferred design-hole limits.

fields.name: liftingPlateWidthMm
fields.doc: Source lifting connections; thread capacity and rigging remain unqualified.

fields.name: minimumClearancePadSide
fields.doc: A centred clearance bore retains the full policy wall on both sides.

fields.name: minimumColumnPadDepth
fields.doc: Joint-pad minimum derived from access, policy edge wall, washer and cover.

types.name: MillCastingKind
types.doc: The five cast bodies of the bench mill; origins are centred on their bottom faces.

types.name: MillCrossSaddle
types.doc: Cross slide with a bottom Z datum and optional through-Y nut tunnel.

types.name: MillCrossTable
types.doc:
T-slot table with integral longitudinal ribs and a recessed X nut bracket seat.
Origin is the underside of the deck; ribs extend down to the guide blocks.

types.name: MillDrawbarLayout
types.doc:
Compact BT30 release study, in the cartridge gauge frame, millimetres.
Interfaces and the force allowance are assumptions pending supplier selection.

types.name: MillDriveHatch
types.doc:
Y drive service hatch. Origin on its front plane; +Y points out of the machine.
Four holes land on dedicated steel anchors rather than the mineral casting.

types.name: MillFixtureAdapter
types.doc: Fabricated plate: four table through holes and four top taps, centred on rectangular patterns.

types.name: MillFrame
types.doc:
Mill structural layout: ribbed base, separate column and finished steel interfaces.
Casting construction and persistence remain in the shared structural components.

types.name: MillFrameInterfaces
types.doc:
Functional datums supplied by the machine using the frame, in millimetres.
Y rails run toward +Y; column rails run toward +Z on a face normal to -Y.

types.name: MillFrameLayout
types.doc:
Mill-specific layout, independent of a particular example and of enclosure size.
Dimensions are a design concept, not material/process or stiffness qualification.

types.name: MillGuidedXYStage
types.doc:
Shared guided cross slide. Drive assemblies attach separately; absent drives
never acquire catalog ratings or implied qualification from the guide model.

types.name: MillLiftingPattern
types.doc:
Four source connections enclose the foundation's nominal centre of mass.
The attachment footprint is a design declaration, never a capacity approval.

fields.name: asCastMass
fields.doc:
Native nominal mass in the pour state: transferred holes and finishing
removal do not yet exist. Embedded anchor hardware remains real components.

types.name: MillMotorCover
types.doc:
Removable three-sided motor hood, open below and toward the coupling (+Y).
Mounting screw details depend on the selected motor cage; 2 mm sheet is assumed.

types.name: MillPanel
types.doc: Rectangular fabricated panel or block, centred in X/Y with its bottom at Z zero.

types.name: MillPedestal
types.doc:
Mill layout on the shared casting/foundation components. Dimensions are conceptual, in mm.
Two chambers and a cross rib retain a front service passage. A steel cap is cast into the roof.

types.name: MillPedestalDetails
types.doc: Pedestal layout intent in mm; openings and the cap engagement are explicit.

types.name: MillPowerDrawbarPart
types.doc:
Separately itemised study hardware, in the cartridge gauge frame. Spring
preload, gripper details and cylinder pressure/force remain selection inputs.

types.name: MillRailFasteners
types.doc:
Install real service screws from the actual placed rail and steel interfaces.
Numerical engagement uses the same source policy as fixtures and anchors.

types.name: MillRailPlacement
types.doc: Shared placement declarations for the axes and their casting-seat holes.

types.name: MillScrewDrive
types.doc:
A supported ball-screw drive: HZMotion fixed motor mount, its floating support, servo and coupling.
Every mounting datum is read from the parts' catalogue and STEP review data; only the coupling
(outside diameter, length, clamps and where it seats) is stated here. Nothing is sized for a load.

fields.name: fixed
fields.doc: Integrated motor mount with the fixed bearing pair.

fields.name: couplingSeat
fields.doc: Motor face to the coupling origin, along the screw.

fields.name: endProfile
fields.doc: HZMotion screw end machined for the fixed mount.

fields.name: bearingDrop
fields.doc: Motor face to fixed-bearing centre.

fields.name: fixedEnd
fields.doc: Screw's fixed end, shoulder to thread: the screw starts `fixed.spec.shoulderZ - fixedEnd` from the motor face.

fields.name: floatingEnd
fields.doc: Screw end to the floating bearing centre: the journal less half the bearing, which seats on its shoulder.

fields.name: floatingBoltZ
fields.doc: Floating support's bolt line and bolt offset.

fields.name: fixedBoltSeat
fields.doc: Bolt counterbore seats above each part's mounting base.

fields.name: m80eBk15
fields.doc: Mill Z: M80E-BK15-C / BF15, braked ELM2H-0750 servo, 48 mm coupling.

types.name: MillScrewPedestal
types.doc: Bearing riser: Z up, +Y toward motor. Rear base bolts leave room for front motor anchors.

types.name: MillServoMount
types.doc:
Horizontal direct-drive cage. +Z goes from pedestal toward motor; +Y is up.
Low anchor holes run through the legs and meet the pedestal's front tapped holes.
Motor receiving pattern follows the 60 mm Leadshine catalog interface.

types.name: MillSpindleBeltGuard
types.doc:
Removable belt enclosure study. The motor carrier closes its rear top;
explicit clearances surround reaction posts, carrier webs and fasteners.

types.name: MillSpindleDrivePart
types.doc:
Editable drive selection carried by the actual mounting plate recipe.
Geometry is a redesign study, not a supplier-qualified mount or enclosure.

fields.name: installed
fields.doc: Shared installed Leadshine selection; belt and carrier remain fabricated parts.

types.name: MillSpindleHead
types.doc:
ATC-ready spindle packaging, independent of the legacy ER20 control model.
Both release joints are inspection motions, not a pneumatic control system.
Supplier release force/stroke, spring sizing and orientation feedback are pending.

types.name: MillSpindleIntegrity
types.doc:
Actual payload geometry and continuous fixed-structure sweeps. Nominal
threads and intended belt/tooth contact are named exclusions, not global skips.

fields.name: checkMotorRemoval
fields.doc: Motor withdrawal after removing its belt, pulley, fasteners and guard.

types.name: MillSpindleMotorLayout
types.doc:
Shared datums of the centered spindle-drive study, in the cartridge gauge
frame. The 440 mm belt and equal 40T HTD5M pulleys give 120 mm centres.

types.name: MillSpindleMotorMount
types.doc:
Braced motor carrier, with a centered two-support option. The legacy offset
recipe remains rebuildable; motor interfaces are explicit study assumptions.

types.name: MillSpindleMotorSupport
MillSpindlePackage
types.doc:
A spindle the Z head carries: the datums the layouts size the head and work envelope from, and the
assembly it installs. Its gauge line sits `seat()` below the head's lower face, on the layout's spindle axis.

fields.name: seat
fields.doc: Gauge line to the head's lower clamping face, mm.

fields.name: diameter
fields.doc: Spindle body diameter where the head clamps it, mm.

fields.name: headHeight
fields.doc: Head block height that clamps this spindle and carries its drive, mm.

fields.name: assembly
fields.doc: Installed spindle for `l`: a `spindle` member whose frame is the gauge line and a `holder` member the tool seats in.

types.name: MillSupportTray
types.doc: Tray with nominal seal clearance around the two bed support strips.

types.name: MillXYDrive
types.doc: An X/Y drive selection: ball nut, screw supports, servo and coupling. `MillXYStageLayout` places the set.

fields.name: bk12
fields.doc: BK12/BF12 supports, preloaded 1605 nut and the ELM2H-0400 servo with a 14/12 coupling.

types.name: MillXYStage
types.doc:
Supported nested Y saddle / X table. Each real prismatic joint drives its screw;
motors and bearing housings stay on their carrying structure, rotors follow the screws.

types.name: MillXYStageIntegrity
types.doc:
Continuous conservative structural sweeps. Y carries the whole X axis, and
table members sweep the Cartesian product of both strokes against the frame.
Intended nut/thread engagement is checked by layout, not a solid box around the nut.
No claim of strength, braking distance or fastener qualification is made here.

types.name: MillXYStageLayout
types.doc:
Mill-specific cross-slide datums. Y moves the saddle; X moves the table.
Positive work coordinates move the workpiece in the negative world direction.
Dimensions and motor patterns are design assumptions, not released vendor drawings.

fields.name: yDrive
fields.doc: HZMotion-supported Y drive; null when Y uses the same BK12 set as X.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: `drive` defaults to `MillXYDrive.bk12()`; `yDrive` replaces it on Y with an HZMotion-supported screw.

types.name: MillYDriveSeat
types.doc:
Steel Y-drive risers, mm. Z up, Y toward motor. Separate receiving holes
match HZMotion's checked pattern; external anchor bores meet the frame insert.
Tap bores are nominal machining requirements, not a joint strength calculation.

types.name: MillYNutBridge
types.doc:
