Gusseted Y nut bridge. Shaft +Z points toward the front, +Y is up.
The upper shoe meets the saddle underside; the vertical flange meets its front.
Rise is measured from the nut axis to the saddle underside. Nominal holes.

types.name: MillYNutDesignChecks
types.doc: Mill-specific assembly intent only. All evaluation is shared with other machines.

types.name: MillYNutMount
types.doc:
Removable front saddle adapter. Native +Z faces forward, +Y is up.
Nut body and flange enter the saddle's underside tunnel. Nominal M5 nut
and M6 saddle interfaces; no tall bridge between screw and saddle.

types.name: MillYTravel
types.doc:
Y working envelope, shared by the frame and cross-slide. Millimetres.
Increasing stroke grows the table and front structure; spindle reach must still
satisfy the rear table/column clearance checked by MillXYStageLayout.

fields.name: railStart
fields.doc:
Covers both the reference BF12 and selected HZMotion BF12 drive.
Round outwards to 10 mm, retaining the requested overrun at both ends.

types.name: MillZAxis
types.doc:
Mechanical Z assembly with one real prismatic joint and a coupled screw.
Includes the stationary braked motor, integrated fixed housing, coupling and
moving carriage/head. Electrical control and spindle payload attach outside.

types.name: MillZAxisIntegrity
types.doc:
Conservative CAD swept envelopes for all translating Z structural parts.
Checks the entire interval against castings, inserts and stationary Z mounts.
Thread engagement, guide contact and spindle/work contact are separate checks;
this is a geometric audit, not a load-capacity or machine safety assessment.

types.name: MillZAxisLayout
types.doc:
Mechanical Z datums, mm. Positive Z raises the head; zero is its top stop.
HZMotion/Leadshine interfaces are pinned; adapter dimensions and loads remain design assumptions.

types.name: MillZBearingPlate
types.doc:
Machined steel crossplate supporting a bearing unit on its rear (+Y) face.
Origin at plate centre X/Y and bottom Z. Mounting holes are nominal clearances.

types.name: MillZCarriage
types.doc:
Welded steel carriage plate and central nut shelf. Origin: rear plate face,
centre X, bottom Z; +Y goes back toward the recessed screw. Nominal holes.

types.name: MillZCouplingGuard
types.doc: Two-bolt removable cover across the front of the open motor stand.

types.name: MillZDriveAdapter
types.doc:
One flat T plate. Origin at column rail tops, centre X/Y.
Rear face +Y supports the pinned M80E STEP base; front M6 blind taps.
Stem clears both rails. Plate strength and casting anchors remain unqualified.

types.name: MillZHead
types.doc:
Ribbed fabricated steel spindle head. Origin on rear mounting face at bottom;
projects toward -Y. Plate/rib thicknesses are explicit design assumptions.

types.name: MillZMotorStand
types.doc:
Steel U stand carries the stationary motor above the upper bearing plate.
Open sides allow access to the coupling and spring-applied shaft brake.
The caller supplies the selected motor hole pitch and pilot recess.

types.name: MillingComponents
types.doc: The milling package's component recipes.

types.name: PneumaticVise
types.doc:
A preset fixed jaw, guided moving jaw, parallels and end stop.
Jaw travel closes the opening; the 6 mm air stroke is separate from the screw preset.
The datum is the fixed jaw face, parallels' top and end stop face.

fields.name: seat
fields.doc: Origin of the preset blank: centred in X/Y, with its bottom on the parallels.

fields.name: load
fields.doc: Release the blank above the parallels, centred in the fully open jaw gap.

fields.name: grippedPosition
fields.doc: Jaw travel at first contact with the preset blank, measured from fully open.

fields.name: stockContacts
fields.doc: Actual members touching correctly seated and clamped stock.

types.name: Rke92Vise
types.doc:
RÖHM RKE92 / 178411 external drawing reference, not imported supplier CAD.
Nominal screw/slide reconstruction is kinematic only: the manufacturer's
mechanical-hydraulic force multiplier is not simulated or assigned a rating.
X across jaws, Y from front of body toward drive, Z from mounting plane.

types.name: Rke92VisePart
types.doc:
Parametric reconstruction, not supplier CAD. RKE92 external dimensions are
published; internal slides, mounting accessories and recesses are nominal.

types.name: SpindleCartridge
types.doc:
ER20 cartridge, origin at its gauge line and body along +Z. Bearing and nose envelopes are
assumed reference dimensions; the gauge line is the controlled point for G43.

types.name: SpindleMotor
types.doc:
Generic 1.1 kW spindle motor rated at 8000 rpm, limited to 10000 rpm. Ratings, inertia and envelope are assumed.
Its drive curve is explicit, so the spindle can use the standard motor/driver binding.

types.name: ZppComponent
types.doc: Reviewed solid groups from pinned supplier STEP. Coordinates: X closes jaws, Y across jaws, Z up.

types.name: ZppWorkholding
types.doc: Supplier workholding on a manual zero-point plate. Pneumatic AR155-I is the mill default; CV15075 remains available.

types.name: AngularContactBearing
types.doc: Angular-contact precision bearing. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: AxisMotor
types.doc:
Mechanical interface of an axis motor. The owning part supplies its dimensions
and mounting tool; builders never infer a servo interface from its body shape.

types.name: AxisServoMotor
types.doc:
Servo housing with its declared mounting flange and pilot. Existing generic
servo envelopes stay unchanged; this part is selected by the linear-axis builder.
The rotating steel shaft is a separate part on the driven joint.

fields.name: massGeometry
fields.doc: Mass of the base motor's body with this flange and pilot, as before the body was drawn in detail.

types.name: BallNut
types.doc:
Generic SFU1605 flanged nut. Dimensions, preload drag and zero reversal clearance are assumed;
they describe a preloaded nut, not an accuracy guarantee for an unpreloaded vendor assembly.

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc: Assumed exterior details; bore, flange face and bolt pattern retain their catalog datums.

types.name: BallScrew
types.doc:
Generic SFU1605 screw. Race root and efficiency are assumed reference values.
The shaft, support critical speed and transmission use the same screw model as sliding screws.

fields.name: RACE_ROOT_DIAMETER
fields.doc: Assumed SFU1605 race root; not a formula for other nominal sizes.

fields.name: ground
fields.doc: Procurement requirement only; ground does not certify a lead-error grade.

types.name: BallScrewRetainer
types.doc:
Generic notched retaining nut and washer, assumed dimensions, not a selected bearing locknut.
Local Z=0 is the motor-side face; the washer bears at Z=5.

types.name: BrakeServo
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class AC servo with spring-applied holding brake. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: massGeometry
fields.doc: Mass of the motor's body with the brake, as before the body was drawn in detail.

types.name: CableChain
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class cable chain. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: geometryAt
fields.doc: Hollow continuous link envelope at a travel position; links and pins are nominal.

fields.name: developedLength
fields.doc: Fixed end at mid-travel; both tangents remain nonnegative at travel limits.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: Centreline in the YZ plane, lower run, 180-degree bend, upper run.

types.name: CasterWheel
types.doc:
Plate-mounted swivel caster: a square top plate, a swivel boss, a fork and a wheel on its axle.
It is one rigid part; the swivel is not a joint. CAD frame: the top of the plate is at z=0 with
the body hanging toward -Z, the swivel axis is the Z axis, the wheel trails it along -X by `trail`
and touches the floor at z = -height. Connectors: `mount` (top of the plate) and `swivel` (axis),
both with +Y along +Z, and `floor` (the contact point, +Y up).

fields.name: height
fields.doc: From the top of the plate to the floor.

fields.name: trail
fields.doc: Horizontal distance from the swivel axis back to the wheel axle.

fields.name: axleHeight
fields.doc: Height of the wheel axle above the floor.

types.name: CrossedRollerBearing
types.doc: Crossed-roller precision bearing. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: DriveWheel
types.doc:
Drive wheel of a wheeled base: a tread disc on a hub boss, bored to sit straight on a motor or
gearbox shaft. CAD frame: the axle runs along +Z, the hub's inner end is at z=0 and the tread
spans z = hubLength..hubLength+width, with a shallow dish in its outer face. Connectors: `bore`
(shaft, at the hub end) and `centre` (axis, mid-tread), both with +Y along +Z. The tread's
floor contact is `radius` from the axle.

types.name: DsgNutHousing
types.doc:
DSG housing: base Y=0, shaft +Z at Y=h, nut flange seats on Z=0.
SFU nut must be rotated 90 degrees about Z so its flats match housing height.
Published tables omit blind thread depths: caller supplies them for clearance/engagement modelling.

types.name: ElectricalSource
types.doc: A part that states the DC voltage available at a supply port.

types.name: ElectricalSupplyRating
types.doc:
Continuous DC output and regenerative absorption capacity. Both power limits
apply to the whole source, shared by every outlet, rather than to each wire.

types.name: EncoderPart
types.doc:
A part that reads a joint's position in counts. `MachineAssembly.addEncoder` puts the result in the
assembly, and rebuilding the assembly asks the part again, so editing an encoder's resolution changes
what the assembly records. Where the encoder sits (on a motor's back shaft, along a rail) comes from
the joint the assembly puts it on.

fields.name: encoder
fields.doc: The encoder `id` on joint `joint`: its kind, counts and index.

types.name: FlangeBearingHousing
types.doc:
Compact flange-style bearing housing: a square flange with a central bore for `bearing` and
four mounting screws around it, all along the bore axis -- the same face/bolt-circle layout as
`NemaStepper`, not a classic two-bolt pillow block whose base is perpendicular to the bore.
CAD frame: mounting face at z=0, flange toward +Z. Connectors: `bore` (axis, mid-depth) for the
bearing, and `bolt1`..`bolt4` (mount), all with +Y along +Z.

fields.name: boltPattern
fields.doc: Bolt centres on the mounting face, counter-clockwise from (+,+).

fields.name: mountScrewPart
fields.doc: Screw that fits the housing's mounting holes.

types.name: Gearbox
types.doc:
A drive-level reduction in an assumed cylindrical housing. Ratio and efficiency are stated
unless explicitly marked assumed. Teeth, shaft bearings, backlash and compliance are not modelled.

types.name: GuideBlockLoad
types.doc: Load transmitted to one block, in the support's local frame. Positions are metres.

types.name: GuideSupport
types.doc:
Reference load sharing for four equal-stiffness blocks on a rigid carriage.
The drive carries force along travel at its measured line of action; the blocks
carry transverse force and the remaining moments. Preload, flexible
castings and unequal block stiffness are not included; the capacity check needs an
explicit safety factor. This calculation is not a bearing-life estimate.

fields.name: utilization
fields.doc: Largest block utilization against an explicitly supplied static rating.

types.name: GuideSupportWrench
types.doc:
A wrench at the centre of a rectangular four-block support. Forces are N, moments N m.
Local X spans the rails, Z follows travel, and Y is normal to the mounting plane.

types.name: HousingStep
types.doc: One coaxial step of a round housing: a cylinder of `diameter` from z0 to z1.

types.name: HzMotionDrawingScrew
types.doc:
Required SFU1605/BK12 and SFU2005/BK15 machining, HZMotion Motor_Bracket.pdf p10.
A procurement/design requirement, not a purchased Vallder screw designation.
Shoulder-to-thread-end E1=36, coupling F1=15, M12x1 over S1=12.
BK12 has a 51 mm fixed end; BK15 has 64 mm (E1=44 + F1=20),
unlike the Vallder standard ends. Race roots are explicit study assumptions.

fields.name: fixedEndFor
fields.doc: Fixed end, shoulder to the thread run-out, for a profile.

fields.name: floatingEndFor
fields.doc: Floating journal length from the screw end.

fields.name: couplingDiameterFor
fields.doc: Coupling journal diameter at the fixed end.

types.name: LeadScrew
types.doc:
Nominal cylindrical envelope of a lead screw. The thread is semantic and shared with its nut;
the flank profile, reliefs and machined ends are not generated.

fields.name: ASSUMED_DAMPING_RATIO
fields.doc: The damping of a steel screw drive, as a ratio of critical damping (assumed: a ball screw shaft rings a little).

fields.name: SUPPORT_BEARING_STIFFNESS
fields.doc: Assumed axial stiffness of the fixed end's support bearings (an angular-contact pair, preloaded), N/mm: about 200 N/um.

fields.name: YOUNGS_MODULUS
fields.doc: Young's modulus of steel, Pa.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc: A screw lies along its axis (+Z), whatever its length.

fields.name: relation
fields.doc: Resolve the coupling from these parts.

fields.name: supportedStiffness
fields.doc:
What the drive gives against axial force, N/mm: the shaft, the nut and the support bearings in series (each a spring
the force passes through, so the compliances add). The nut and bearing values are catalogue-typical and assumed.

fields.name: axialStiffness
fields.doc:
Shaft-only axial stiffness, N/mm, from the race root and full shaft length.
Nut and support compliance must be supplied by a measured transmission override.

fields.name: axialRigidityAt
fields.doc: Axial rigidity EA at a shaft station, N.

fields.name: axialComplianceBetween
fields.doc: Shaft compliance between physical bearing/nut stations, mm/N.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: A supplier-specific end profile may provide its own BOM designation.

types.name: LeadScrewNut
types.doc:
ACME/trapezoidal lead screw nut: a flanged block with a bore matching the screw diameter and
a mounting bolt pattern on the flange face, for driving a carriage. The thread itself is
semantic (`LeadScrewThread` family, diameter, pitch, starts and hand), not modelled.
`travelPerRevolution()`/`rotationFor()` convert between screw rotation and nut travel; for a
right-hand thread, positive rotation about +Z moves the nut toward -Z.
CAD frame: axis along +Z, body from z=0 to z=bodyLength, flange from there to
z=bodyLength+flangeThickness. Connectors: `bore` (axis, mid-body) and `mount1`..`mountN` (on
the flange face), all with +Y along +Z.

fields.name: flanged
fields.doc: A barrel nut has no flange and is retained by its bracket.

fields.name: backlash
fields.doc: Assumed reversal clearance, mm: plain bronze 0.15, preloaded 0.05, ball nut 0.01.

fields.name: drag
fields.doc: Assumed running torque, N m, including nut preload and support bearing drag.

fields.name: axialStiffness
fields.doc:
Assumed axial stiffness of the nut, N/mm (catalogue-typical rigidity of a 16 mm class ball nut: about 100 N/um unpreloaded, 300 N/um
preloaded). A sliding nut is taken as rigid against the shaft (null): its thread stiffness is far above the screw's.

fields.name: efficiency
fields.doc: Sliding nuts use a greased steel/bronze friction of 0.1; ball nuts assume 90% efficiency.

fields.name: boltPattern
fields.doc: Mount bolt centres on the flange face, counter-clockwise from angle 0.

fields.name: travelPerRevolution
fields.doc: Signed axial travel for one positive screw revolution.

fields.name: rotationFor
fields.doc: Screw rotation, in radians, needed to travel `distance`.

fields.name: mountScrewPart
fields.doc: Screw that fits the nut's mounting holes.

types.name: LeadScrewNutKind
types.doc: Generic nut families; their allowances are assumptions, not vendor ratings.

fields.name: BALL_EFFICIENCY
fields.doc: Assumed rolling efficiency for the generic ball-race family.

fields.name: lead
fields.doc: Positive axial distance per revolution, independent of handedness.

fields.name: raceRootDiameter
fields.doc: Explicit catalogue or assumed race root, mm; required for ball screws.

fields.name: signedLead
fields.doc:
Signed nut travel for one positive screw revolution about the screw's +Z axis.
A right-hand thread moves the nut toward -Z; a left-hand thread moves it toward +Z.

fields.name: threadSpec
fields.doc: The common face-thread value retains this family's profile and positive lead.

types.name: LeadScrewThreadFamily
types.doc:
Semantic lead-screw thread. Dimensions are nominal millimetres; this does not validate
that a diameter/pitch combination is listed in a particular edition of a thread standard.

fields.name: Ball
fields.doc: Recirculating ball race; pitch is the axial lead for a single start.

types.name: LeadshineServo
types.doc:
50–7500 W ELM1/ELM2, 220/380 VAC. Face at z=0, housing -Z, separate rotating shaft +Z.
Interfaces follow datasheet pp. 3–16; extrusion, rear cover and connector shapes are approximations.
E = brake, F = no brake. ELM1 uses magnetic feedback, ELM2 optical; both are 23 bit.

types.name: LeadshineServoLargeCatalog
types.doc:
Larger ELM2 rows transcribed from LeadshineServo.SOURCE pp. 7–16.
Keep winding, inertia class and connector suffix in each designation.

types.name: LeadshineServoSpec
types.doc: Leadshine ELM1/ELM2 drawing dimensions, mm; catalog currents in Arms, speeds in rpm.

types.name: LeadshineTorqueCurve
types.doc: Raster evidence is distinct from a verified motor capability. Speeds are rpm.

types.name: LeadshineTorqueCurveData
types.doc: Generated by examples/spindle-drive-study/digitize_curves.py.

fields.name: all
fields.doc: Fresh records so callers cannot mutate shared qualification state.

fields.name: studyCurve
fields.doc: Only identified variants are eligible for an explicitly conditional study.

fields.name: studyTorque
fields.doc:
Returns null outside the graph; never extrapolate torque beyond captured speeds.
Reading allowance is subtracted for a conservative ordinate, but does not bound
unknown drive/cooling conditions or uncertainty in a schematic graph's axes.

fields.name: qualifiedContinuousTorque
fields.doc: Qualification requires both exact variant match and verified operating conditions.

types.name: LimitSwitch
types.doc: Housing, lever and roller envelope. Local +Z is the approaching trigger direction.

types.name: LimitSwitchSpec
types.doc: Assumed generic roller micro-switch; catalog dimensions are not vendor claims.

types.name: LinearBearing
types.doc:
LM-series linear ball bearing, for a round rail. Unlike `Bushing`, sizes come from a fixed
catalog rather than a proportional formula.
CAD frame: axis along +Z, front face at z=0, back face at z=length, matching
`DeepGrooveBearing`. Connectors: `front`, `back` (faces) and `axis` (mid-length), all with +Y
along +Z.

fields.name: guideRodDiameter
fields.doc: Diameter of the round guide rod for a named shaft fit. The allowance is diametral.

fields.name: housingSeatDiameter
fields.doc: Diameter of the carriage seat for a named housing fit. The allowance is diametral.

fields.name: housingSeat
fields.doc: Cylindrical carriage seat tool for this bearing and housing fit.

types.name: LinearBearingSpec
types.doc: LM-series linear ball bearing boundary dimensions in millimetres.

types.name: LinearGuideSystem
types.doc:
The paired round-rod guide used by a linear axis.

This value object keeps the bearing catalog row, rod journal fit, carriage seat fit and
resulting guide rods together. It does not add an assembly root by itself; callers place the
two rods and mate the two bearings through their own assembly model.

fields.name: forRailProfile
fields.doc: Construct a profile-rail guide as an alternative to the paired round-rod system.

fields.name: validateCarriage
fields.doc: Check the carriage envelope against both bearing seats and the bearing body length.

types.name: LinearRail
types.doc:
A cut length of profile rail for a catalogue carriage. Its drawing is one of two, chosen explicitly and saved with
it: `nominal`, the catalogue section with grooves (`ProfileRailShapes`), or `measured`, the running section taken
from the pinned HIWIN CAD (HG rails). The drawing changes neither its part number nor its datasheet mass. Mounting
holes are counterbored from the rail table and expose named connectors. CAD frame: the cross-section is centred
on x=0, spans y=-railHeight..0, and runs along +Z.

fields.name: drawing
fields.doc: `NOMINAL` or `MEASURED`.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc: Runs along +Z with its top (+Y) up, whatever its cut length.

fields.name: metric
fields.doc:
The rail for carriage `profile`, drawn `measured` where the pinned CAD has its section and `nominal` otherwise,
unless `drawing` says which.

fields.name: mountingHole
fields.doc: The rail table's counterbored mounting hole.

fields.name: measuredSection
fields.doc:
The undrilled running section of HG rail `rail` from the pinned CAD, `length` long along +Z. Supplier STEP
endpoints differ by up to 0.00000024 mm (HGR45R): segments weld within that tolerance, never across a gap.

types.name: LinearRailBlock
types.doc:
A catalogue carriage block. Its drawing is chosen explicitly and saved with it: `nominal`, the catalogue outline
with end caps and tapped holes (`ProfileRailShapes`), or `supplier`, the pinned HIWIN CAD of HG carriages, loaded
on demand from the prepared reference directory. The drawing changes neither its part number nor its datasheet
mass. The four mounting holes and the rail axis are interface data from the catalogue. CAD frame: centred on
z=0, rail top at y=0, mounting face at blockHeight - railHeight.

fields.name: drawing
fields.doc: `NOMINAL` or `SUPPLIER`.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc: Riding on its rail: mounting face (+Y) up and the travel (Z) running across the view.

fields.name: mountThreadDepth
fields.doc: Full depth of the tapped mounting holes where the table gives it; HGW tables give only the thread.

fields.name: referenceDirectory
fields.doc: The prepared HG reference directory: `MATERIA_HG_REFERENCE`, else build/suppliers/vallder/hg-reference in the repository.

fields.name: supplierCad
fields.doc: Pinned HG model `model` (carriage or rail), checked against its review digest and frame. The caller owns it.

types.name: LinearRailBore
types.doc: Counterbored rail mounting hole from the rail table: through bore d, counterbore D and depth h, in mm.

types.name: LinearRailProfileSpec
types.doc:
A profile-rail carriage and the rail it runs on, in mm and kg. `designation` names the carriage (HGH15CA, MGN12C)
and `rail` the rail (HGR15R, MGNR12R); every carriage on one rail repeats that rail's fields.

types.name: LinearRailRating
types.doc:
One published load rating of a carriage, as its source states it: basic dynamic (C) and static (C0) load ratings
in N, and static rated moments in N·m where the source gives them. Sizing applies its own static safety factor
to `staticLoad`; no derating is folded in here.

types.name: LinearRailSystem
types.doc:
Catalog-backed profile-rail guide assembly. This is an alternative to the round-rod
`LinearGuideSystem`: the rail is fixed and one or more blocks travel along its axis. Rows are
keyed by carriage designation; each names its rail, the tables it comes from, and the load
ratings published for it.

fields.name: catalog
fields.doc: Profile-rail carriages and their rails: HIWIN MGN miniature guides and the HG family.

fields.name: rating
fields.doc: The rating sizing uses: the first one listed, the purchase source's.

fields.name: forProfile
fields.doc: Construct a rail and one or more matching blocks from a catalog designation.

fields.name: assembly
fields.doc:
Build a kinematic guide model with one prismatic joint per block. Joint coordinates are
measured from the rail's axis connector and constrained to the usable stroke.

fields.name: setTravel
fields.doc: Move one block to a distance along the rail.

fields.name: components
fields.doc: Components and stable instance ids for geometry exporters.

types.name: LinearScale
types.doc:
A linear scale laid along a rail, read by a head on the carriage: `countsPerMillimetre` counts a
millimetre of the carriage's travel, with a reference mark at the joint's zero when it has an index.
It is a load-side encoder: it sees where the carriage is, whatever the drive stretches or lost.
The strip is 10 mm by 2 mm, an assumption. CAD frame: along +Z from z=0 to `length`, like a linear
rail. Connectors: `axis` and `mount` at the start of the strip.

types.name: MotionComponents
types.doc: The motion package's component recipes.

types.name: MotorBody
types.doc:
A square-flanged motor housing as servo and spindle motors are built: a flange of side `face` and thickness
`flange` with bolt holes, a housing with chamfered corners, a rear (encoder) cap, and a connector boss on the
housing's +Y side. Motor CAD frame: mounting face at z = 0, body towards -Z over `length`; the shaft is its own
part. Everything lies inside the box `face` × `face` × `length` behind the face, the motor's envelope.

types.name: MotorBrakeSpec
types.doc: Physical spring-applied brake data, independent of the controller release policy.

types.name: MotorDrive
types.doc:
A motor part that can drive an assembly joint. The part states its drive kind and what it can
deliver; `MachineAssembly.addMotor` puts the result in the assembly, and rebuilding the assembly
asks the part again, so editing a motor's ratings changes its actuator. A servo motor part
implements this the same way a stepper does.

fields.name: electricalRating
fields.doc: Winding data for a servo; steppers use their own pull-out/current model.

types.name: MotorDriver
types.doc:
A motor amplifier and its settings. The generic envelopes and ratings are assumptions,
not verified product specifications. A stated voltage is used only without a wired supply.

types.name: NemaFrameInterface
types.doc: Nominal NEMA frame mounting interface in millimetres. Motor bodies and shafts vary by model.

types.name: NemaStepper
types.doc:
Stepper motor built from a NEMA mounting interface and a named motor variant.
CAD frame: mounting face at z=0, body toward -Z, shaft along +Z.

fields.name: spec
fields.doc: Frame mounting dimensions; kept as `spec` for existing callers.

fields.name: ratingCatalog
fields.doc:
Ratings of the named variants. Holding torque and rated current are the ones the products are
named by; inductance and rotor inertia are typical datasheet values, not checked against
the linked pages.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: Named manufacturer variant.

fields.name: custom
fields.doc: Build a motor from explicit frame and motor dimensions without a named catalog recipe.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc: Default named variant for a frame. A length override creates a generic preview variant.

fields.name: rating
fields.doc: The motor's ratings, or null for a variant without them, such as a generic length.

fields.name: pullOutTorque
fields.doc:
Pull-out torque at shaft speed `speed` (rad/s) on a `volts` supply, in N m: the holding torque
until the winding's inductance keeps its current below rated, then falling as 1 / speed. A
first-order model: back EMF, the driver's current regulation and resonance are left out.

fields.name: usableTorque
fields.doc:
Torque and speed the motor can be relied on for on a `volts` supply: `margin` of its holding
torque, up to the speed where its pull-out torque falls to that. Half is the usual margin
that keeps a stepper from missing steps.

fields.name: pullOutCurve
fields.doc:
The pull-out curve as torque-speed points (speed in rad/s, torque in N m, alternating): the
holding torque to the corner speed, then falling as 1 / speed. Points are close enough to the
hyperbola that joining them by lines overstates it by about 1% at most, and the curve ends at
the usable speed or eight times the corner, whichever is higher.

fields.name: boltPattern
fields.doc: Bolt centres on the mounting face, counter-clockwise from (+,+).

fields.name: mountingCutout
fields.doc: Cutting tool for a plate in front of the face (z=0..thickness): pilot and bolt clearances.

types.name: OpenBuildsNema23Geometry
types.doc:
Adapted from Gumyr's bd_warehouse, Apache-2.0.
See machinekit/third-party/bd_warehouse/NOTICE for pinned source and changes.

types.name: PillowBlock
types.doc:
Base-mounted UCP-style pillow block unit. The housing is a cast base with two mounting
holes along the housing length and an insert-bearing envelope above the base. CAD frame: the
shaft runs along +Z, its centre is at `shaftHeight`, the base bottom is y=0, length runs along
X, and base width runs along Z. Connectors:
`axis` at the shaft centre, `input`/`output` at the housing ends, `base` on the mounting face,
and `bolt1`/`bolt2` at the two mounting-hole centres.

types.name: PillowBlockSpec
types.doc: Catalog dimensions for a base-mounted UCP-style pillow block unit, in mm.

types.name: PlanetaryReducer
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class planetary reducer. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc:
The envelope is the bored housing cylinder. The preview has an input adapter at z = 0, the planetary housing
and a bolted output flange at the far end, around the bore.

fields.name: massGeometry
fields.doc: Its mass is that of the plain bored housing (the drawn steps and holes do not set it).

fields.name: outputDeflection
fields.doc: SI torsional stiffness on the reducer output shaft.

types.name: PowerSupply
types.doc:
A DC supply with stated output ratings and an assumed rectangular envelope.
Current is a DC output rating shared by all outlets. A regenerative rating
represents an integrated shunt and braking resistor, with an assumed envelope.

types.name: PrecisionError
types.doc:
A stated error bound, not an injected waveform. Units and interpretation travel with it.
Runout bounds are TIR; eccentricity and cogging are amplitudes.

types.name: PrecisionErrors
types.doc: Typed component facet, persisted through each component's recipe inputs.

fields.name: inAssembly
fields.doc: Path-qualified readout, including nested assemblies, without recentering or applying errors.

types.name: PrecisionRotaryAxis
types.doc: RA-D8: interchangeable bought and built rotary axes, without exposing their internal parts.

types.name: ProfileRailShapes
types.doc:
Nominal profile-rail and carriage-block shapes from catalogue data (`LinearRail.NOMINAL`, the nominal carriage).
Rail frame: section centred on x = 0, y from -railHeight to the rail top at 0, running along +Z. Block frame:
rail-facing side at y = 0, top at blockHeight - railHeight, centred on z = 0. Rail bores come from the rail table,
carriage threads from the socket-head cap screw catalogue.

fields.name: rail
fields.doc:
The rail: its rectangular section with chamfered top edges and a ball-track groove along each side (two on
four-row HG-type profiles, one on MGN-type miniature ones), and counterbored mounting holes at `holes` (z).

fields.name: block
fields.doc:
The carriage block above the rail top: a steel body with chamfered top edges, plastic end caps and seals at
both ends, and four tapped mounting holes at the catalogue's spacings across and along the rail.

types.name: ProximitySwitch
types.doc: Assumed generic M8/M12 inductive sensor envelope, with an explicit sensing gap.

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc:
The envelope is the barrel's cylinder. The preview has a connector end at the mount (z = 0), a fine-pitch
metric threaded barrel (a cosmetic thread, M8x1 or M12x1) and the sensing cap at the face (z = length).

fields.name: massGeometry
fields.doc: Its mass is that of the plain barrel cylinder (the drawn connector and cap do not set it).

types.name: PurchasedRotaryPart
types.doc:
One purchased unit, split into fixed/rotating envelopes solely for kinematics.
The rotor is included in the unit's BOM; no internal bearing/motor construction is invented.

types.name: PurchasedRotaryTable
types.doc: Purchased DD rotary axis with the same mount/work/C contract as a built table.

types.name: ReducerSpec
types.doc: Input/output shaft reduction, independent of its housing geometry.

types.name: RotaryAxisSpec
types.doc: RA-D8 machine-independent rotary-axis data. Every numeric input retains its own provenance.

types.name: RotaryEncoderRing
types.doc: Rotary ring encoder. Reference row is Assumed; dimensions are simplified envelopes.

types.name: RoundHousing
types.doc:
A round housing along +Z as reducers, gearboxes and encoders are built: coaxial steps (flanges, body, adapters),
an optional through bore, and bolt holes through one flange on a circle. Every step lies inside the cylinder of
the largest diameter over the steps' span, the part's envelope.

fields.name: part
fields.doc:
`holes` bolt holes of `holeDiameter` on a circle of `holeCircle` diameter, drilled through the step at index
`holeStep`; none when `holes` is zero. `bore` zero leaves the housing solid.

types.name: ScrewNutDimensions
types.doc: Explicit flange dimensions, mm, for catalogue nuts with independently specified geometry.

types.name: ScrewSupport
types.doc:
How one end of a lead screw is held, for its bending. A screw driven through a rigid coupling
from a motor is held (`Fixed`) at that end. A bearing that carries radial load but lets the
end tilt is `Simple`; a pair of bearings, or a bearing with a long fit, is `Fixed`; an end with
no bearing is `Free`.

types.name: ScrewSupportUnit
types.doc:
Generic BK12 fixed and BF12 floating bearing units. Millimetre envelopes and bearing seats
are assumed reference dimensions; the support condition is the mechanical beam boundary.
Origin is at the shaft centre; the shaft runs along +Z and the foot is at y=-25.

fields.name: axialStiffness
fields.doc: Assumed catalogue-typical axial rigidity of the preloaded fixed pair, N/mm; floating supports carry no axial load.

types.name: ServoElectricalLoad
types.doc:
Conservative simultaneous peak demand, without assuming that axes take turns
accelerating. The source and amplifier support this indefinitely; motor rated
torque remains the planner's thermal limit. Currents here are phase RMS for
the amplifier and DC for the source, never interchanged.

types.name: ServoElectricalRating
ServoMotor
types.doc:
A servo motor: rated and peak torque, rated and maximum speed, rotor inertia and the encoder counts
of its own feedback. Its actuator is a servo drive, so a planner relies on its peak torque and
maximum speed and its rated torque bounds the average (see `PlanCheck`). Usually it drives a joint
through a `Gearbox`.

The named ratings are generic: round numbers in the range of the 3000 rpm AC servo families made at 50,
100, 200, 400 and 750 W (rated torque is power over 3000 rpm, peak three times that, 5000 rpm at most, a little
under 20 bits' worth of encoder). They are assumptions, not a vendor's datasheet.
CAD frame: mounting face at z=0, body toward -Z, shaft along +Z. Connectors: `mountFace`, `shaftAxis`.

types.name: ServoMounting
types.doc:
Mounting face at Z=0; hole coordinates are in that face, dimensions in mm.
Null mounting data means the interface has not been specified.

types.name: ServoRating
types.doc: What a servo motor can deliver, in SI units: torques in N m, speeds in rad/s, inertia in kg m².

types.name: SfuDrawingScrew
types.doc:
Vallder's published SFU20/SFU25 standard ends, shared by the 5/10 mm lead variants.
Semantic race; root envelope for the lock thread. Small chamfers/fillets omitted.
Root diameter is an explicit engineering assumption. Catalogue end option, not custom machining.

types.name: SfuNut
types.doc:
Shared SFU flange family; published per-model dimensions, exact hole clearances and flats.
Root diameter is an explicit engineering input, not inferred from nominal size/lead.

types.name: ShaftBrakePart
types.doc:
Assumed 4 N m spring-applied shaft brake. The hub and disc rotate with the motor;
front, shell and back sectors attach to its mount. Separate sectors keep their convex
collision hulls clear of the shaft and released disc. Dimensions are mm, delays seconds.
These envelopes, steel mass allocation and ratings are reference values, not vendor data.

fields.name: sectorCount
fields.doc: Fewest sectors whose convex inner chord clears the actual rotating radius.

types.name: ShaftCoupling
types.doc:
Rigid sleeve coupling joining two shaft ends, with an independent bore on each side (a
reducer coupling when they differ). Preview includes configurable radial tapped holes for
the semantic set screws; Envelope keeps the turned sleeve and bores only.
CAD frame: axis along +Z, side A face at z=0, side B face at z=length, matching
`DeepGrooveBearing`. Connectors: `sideA`, `sideB` (faces) and `axis` (mid-length), all with
+Y along +Z.

fields.name: componentType
fields.doc: Subclasses must declare their own recipe and saved values.

fields.name: setScrewPart
fields.doc: Set screw that clamps the coupling to a shaft.

fields.name: billOfMaterials
fields.doc: Coupling BOM, optionally including one semantic set screw for each radial hole.

types.name: ShaftCouplingSetScrew
types.doc:
One radial tapped set-screw hole in a shaft coupling. `z` is the axial location and `angle`
is measured in radians from local +X toward +Y. The thread flanks are not modelled.

types.name: ShaftDetail
types.doc: Optional manufacturing details for a stepped shaft.

types.name: ShaftEncoder
types.doc:
A rotary encoder that rides a shaft end, such as a stepper's back shaft: the housing a standard
optical encoder gives, reading `countsPerRevolution` quadrature counts a turn, optionally with an
index pulse once a turn. On a motor's own joint it is a motor-side encoder, which sees lost steps.
Sizes are those of a typical 38 mm housing, assumptions rather than a catalogue part.
CAD frame: mounting face at z=0, housing toward +Z, shaft axis along Z. Connectors: `mount` (the
face to put against the motor's back) and `axis`.

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc:
The envelope is the housing cylinder. The preview has a clamping flange at the mount, the housing, a rear
cover and the hollow bore it rides the shaft on.

fields.name: massGeometry
fields.doc: Its mass is that of the plain housing cylinder (the drawn flange, cover and bore do not set it).

types.name: ShaftGroove
types.doc:
A full-depth retaining-ring groove from `z0` to `z0 + width`, cut to `diameter`.
A `name` connector (axis, groove mid-width) is added when given, for mating a `RetainingRing`.

types.name: ShaftKeyway
types.doc:
A keyway cut for `key`, starting at `z0` and running the key's length.
Adds a `name` connector at the seat floor, mid-keyway, for mating the key with a fixed joint.

types.name: ShaftSection
types.doc: One constant-diameter length of a stepped shaft, in millimetres.

types.name: ShaftShoulderDetail
types.doc: Detail applied at a section shoulder. The relief diameter is the finished root diameter.

types.name: ShaftThreadEnd
types.doc: Semantic thread specification for a machined shaft end. Thread flanks are not modelled.

types.name: SteppedShaft
types.doc:
Coaxial cylindrical sections stacked along +Z, producing square shoulders at each diameter
change. CAD frame: input end at z=0, output end at z=totalLength.
Connectors: `input` (axis, z=0), `output` (shaft, z=totalLength), plus any `namedFaces` (axis,
for bearing or collar seats), one connector per named keyway, and one per named groove. Keyways
are cut on the shaft's local +Y side, so a `ParallelKey` mated through the keyway's connector
sits flush in the slot; groove connectors are axial, for a `RetainingRing`.

fields.name: diameterAt
fields.doc: Diameter of the section containing `z`; a boundary belongs to the following section.

fields.name: journalDiameterAt

types.doc:
Assumed gravity-return contact finger. Its stock datum is z=0, its hinge is
50 mm behind the front face and 20 mm below the datum. The top projects 1 mm
above the datum so thin stock can engage it after the finger drops.
Frictionless stock registration and contact compliance are explicit simulation
assumptions, not material ratings.

fields.name: DROP_ANGLE

Assumed 4/3 hydraulic valve block: agreeing coils close every work port.
P is the regulated feed, T the tank return, and A/B the cylinder work outlets.

fields.doc: Alternating lower/upper material crossings; called strictly between curve events.

fields.name: projection
fields.doc: Material projection onto X inside an open Y strip; holes are filled only if material exists elsewhere in that strip.

types.name: PressSheetPose
types.doc: Native-free sheet placement at one air-bending stroke sample.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: Conserve the developed strip while keeping its concave midpoint under the punch.

fields.name: manufactured
fields.doc: Actual stock contact geometry is independent of a planner's learned depth correction.

types.name: PressStationGeometry
types.doc: Contact datums of one installed station in the open press frame, in mm.

types.name: PressStrokeCollision
types.doc: Check actual material through every sampled stroke pose against all installed tooling and machine volumes.

fields.name: check
fields.doc: Named diagnoses carry authored identities and the sampled angle, never parsed prism labels.

types.name: PressStrokeCollisionResult
types.doc: Physical interference and insufficient geometric resolution remain distinct search outcomes.

types.name: PressToolContact
types.doc: Exact sections remain attached to a typed installed tooling owner.

types.name: PressToolDatum
types.doc: Representative installed contact members for one homogeneous tooling station.

types.name: PressTravel
types.doc: A finite travel interval in mm. A fixed optional axis has equal endpoints.

types.name: PressWallPrismQuery
types.doc: Exact line/arc wall extrusion against a convex obstacle at any relative orientation.

types.name: SheetBodyGeometry
types.doc: Fixed material patches for rigid simulation bodies; geometry and mass come from the developed stock.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc: Body axes follow the patch centroid tangent; local collision geometry and inertia stay fixed.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: Tangent-patch error includes curvature, thickness mapping and authored boundary chords.

types.name: SheetCollisionQuery
types.doc: Narrow convex material boundary; curved-contact refinement remains in the press queries.

fields.name: separation
fields.doc: Signed separation in mm; a positive support gap is a lower bound on material distance.

types.name: SheetGrip
types.doc: A grip belongs to authored wall material, at wall-local coordinates on one stock face.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc: The grip frame follows wall FK; its normal always points away from stock material.

types.name: SheetPrismProfile
types.doc: Wall material decomposed into convex extrusions. Holes remain empty; arcs have an explicit chord error.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: Vertical material slabs preserve all loops without bridging a hole or taking a filled hull.

types.name: Extruder
types.doc:
The geared extruder body: housing, hobbed drive gear and spring idler. The reduction is not part of it: the
motor's pinion and the gear on the drive shaft are spur gears of the assembly, and the drive gear's angle is
what the extruder joint plans. Origin: the filament path at the grip, on the housing's front face (the side the
nozzle is on), filament along +Z downwards towards -Z; the drive shaft runs along +Y behind it.

fields.name: rotationPerMillimetre
fields.doc: Radians the hobbed gear turns for each millimetre of filament it feeds.

fields.name: filamentPerRadian
fields.doc: Millimetres of filament for each radian of the drive gear.

types.name: Fan
types.doc:
A DC fan or blower. Origin: the middle of the underside of the housing, with the fan's axis along +Z. A
blower's outlet is the face on +X; `outlet` is there. Rows are assumed 24 V parts.

types.name: HeatedBed
types.doc:
A heated bed: an aluminium plate with a silicone heater under it. Origin: the middle of the plate's top
face, whose normal is +Z; `surface` is there. The plate's underside carries `mount`.

types.name: HeaterCartridge
types.doc: A resistive cartridge heater. Its resistance follows from its rating: R = V^2 / P.

fields.name: power
fields.doc: The power it draws on `supply` volts, in watts.

types.name: HeaterControlPolicy
types.doc: One immutable policy, applied to each heater's own heat capacity, power and loss.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc:
C dT/dt = P*duty - loss*(T-room); tau=C/loss, kp=C/(P*lambda), ki=kp/Ti.
There is no derivative term: this assumed block has no transport delay to lead.

types.name: HeaterControlPolicySpec
types.doc:
Authored choices for a first-order thermal block's PI controller and fault monitoring.
Every field is required. This policy describes the assumed plant; a controller with
transport delay or different thermal dynamics needs its own tuning.

types.name: Hotend
types.doc:
A hotend without its nozzle, cartridge or thermistor, which are separate parts: a heatsink and the heater block they
clamp to. All thermal and flow values are assumptions for a V6-style hotend, to be replaced by a measured part.
Origin: the block's underside on the nozzle axis, which runs along +Z; `nozzleSeat` is there, `filamentEntry` is at
the top of the heatsink and the cartridge and thermistor seats are in the block.

fields.name: loss
fields.doc: Heat leaving the block at `celsius` above `ambient` with the part-cooling fan at `fanDuty` (0 to 1), watts.

fields.name: maxSpeed
fields.doc: The fastest filament speed the melt zone delivers through a bead of `area` m^2, m/s of travel: flow over area.

types.name: KlipperConfig
types.doc:
A Klipper `printer.cfg` for a printer, as text, and a reader of what it says. The pins are placeholders (`PIN_X_STEP`,
...) that name what a board must wire; `pins` lists them with their meaning, and Klipper refuses the file until each
is replaced, which is what a config for a board that has not been chosen should do. Lengths are millimetres.

fields.name: PID_SCALE
fields.doc: Klipper keeps PID gains times 255, as a duty of 0 to 255.

fields.name: number
fields.doc: A number as the config writes it: no more digits than mean anything, none trailing.

fields.name: scaled
fields.doc: The controller's gain as Klipper writes it.

fields.name: pins
fields.doc: The pins a board must supply, each with what it is for, in the order the file uses them.

fields.name: pinReport
fields.doc: The pin report as text: one line per placeholder, what it is and where the file uses it.

fields.name: parse
fields.doc:
A config as its sections and their keys (a Klipper section header is `[name]` or `[kind name]`; keys are
`key: value` or `key = value`; comments start with `#` or `;`). Enough to read back what `render` writes.

types.name: KlipperExtruder
types.doc: The extruder: its stepper's gearing, the filament and nozzle it feeds and the heater that melts it.

types.name: KlipperHeater
types.doc: A heater: Klipper's PID gains are the controller's, scaled by 255 (see `scaled`).

types.name: KlipperPrinter
types.doc: Everything a CoreXY printer's `printer.cfg` states that the machine's model knows.

types.name: KlipperProbe
types.doc: A probe beside the nozzle: where it stands relative to it and the nozzle's height above the bed when it trips.

types.name: KlipperStepper
types.doc: One stepper of a Klipper printer: what its `[stepper_x]` section says.

types.name: Nozzle
types.doc: A brass M6 nozzle. Origin: the orifice, with the nozzle standing up along +Z; `tip` is there.

fields.name: orificeArea
fields.doc: Cross-section of the orifice, mm^2.

types.name: PrintMaterialSpec
types.doc:
Feedstock and its process-response parameters for a chosen extrusion setup.
Diameter is metres, minimum extrusion temperature is Celsius and melt lag is
seconds. Lag depends on the material/hotend combination, not just polymer name.
This specification does not imply a verified material or hardware compatibility.

fields.name: minExtrusionTemperature
fields.doc: Zero explicitly disables the cold-extrusion threshold.

fields.name: assumedPla175
fields.doc: Retains the printer example's existing unmeasured assumptions; not a vendor material profile.

types.name: PrintedPart
types.doc:
The part being printed, where the simulation lays it: a marker the size of a bead at the machine's zero, the bed's
front left corner at its surface, which the print replaces with the material it deposits. Origin: that corner, the
surface's normal along +Z. The mass is that of the marker; the deposit adds none to the simulation.

types.name: PrintingComponents
types.doc: The printing package's component recipes.

types.name: Thermistor
types.doc: An NTC temperature sensor. Rows are assumed values for the common 100k, beta 3950 part.

fields.name: resistance
fields.doc: The sensor's resistance at a temperature, in ohms.

fields.name: temperature
fields.doc: The temperature a resistance reads, in degrees C.

types.name: ThermistorSpec
types.doc: Beta-model NTC thermistor: R = R25 * exp(beta * (1/T - 1/T25)), T in kelvin.

types.name: ArcTorchControl
EndEffectorControl
types.doc: One digital control of an end effector: the channel that works it and the inlet it drives.

fields.name: Arc
fields.doc: An arc torch's trigger: the channel that lights its arc and the control inlet it drives.

fields.name: Driver
fields.doc: Start, reverse, program selection and vacuum are worked by the screwdriving process.

types.name: EndEffectorControls
types.doc:
What it takes to run an end effector, read from the facets its parts declare: the digital
controls that work its gripper, vacuum and changer lock, each on a channel named
`<prefix>/<member>.<action>`; the vacuum pressure sensor, if it has one, as
`<prefix>/<member>.<signal port>`; where its suction cups touch; and its arc torches, each with
the arc channel `<prefix>/<member>.arc` and, with it, the wire speed, voltage and weld sensor of an
`ArcTorchControl`. Each control drives a consumer inlet of the right
service that its configuration supplies. A runtime, real or simulated, binds these; nothing here
depends on one.

fields.name: arcChannel
fields.doc: The first arc torch's channel, or null when the effector has none.

fields.name: vacuumChannel
fields.doc: The vacuum control's channel, or null when the effector has none.

fields.name: gripperChannel
fields.doc: A physical gripper's logical close channel, by its assembly member ID.

types.name: GripperContact
types.doc: Physical jaws, their grasp-state switch, and the connector at the finger workspace.

types.name: RobotScene
types.doc:
The robot records of a scene, read from the facets of a machine's parts: the tools its end
effector works and the sensors it carries. MachineKit says what the parts are; this says how a
robot runtime sees them.

fields.name: robotTools
fields.doc:
A robot's tools as its end effector `tool` declares them, its members' occurrences under
`prefix`: each suction cup's contact, worked by the effector's vacuum control channel and
reporting on its pressure sensor when it has one.

fields.name: robotSensors
fields.doc:
The sensors `robot` declares, its members' occurrences under `prefix`: planar scanners and the
screwdriver's calibrated digital contact input at its TCP.

types.name: ScrewdriverControl
types.doc:
Spindle control and sensed feed, derived from the mounted carrier and its bit.
Start and vacuum are digital; direction is digital (true reverses), and program
is an integral analogue slot number, with zero meaning no selected program.

types.name: SuctionContact
types.doc: Where a suction cup meets what it holds: its member and its contact connector.

types.name: ToolAxisReach
types.doc: Design-only reach check for a named TCP and axis, with joint limits and free roll.

fields.signature: (state:AssemblyState, joints:Array<String>, limits:Array<{lower:Float, upper:Float}>, target:{x:Float, y:Float, z:Float}, direction:{x:Float, y:Float, z:Float}, seed:Array<Float>, occurrence:String, connector:String, ?xDirection:{x:Float, y:Float, z:Float}, ?residualTolerance:Float):Null<Array<Float>>
fields.doc: The joint values that put the tip on `target` with the wire along `direction`, or null.

fields.name: solveFrame
fields.signature: (state:AssemblyState, joints:Array<String>, limits:Array<{lower:Float, upper:Float}>, target:materia.assembly.AssemblyRecord.AssemblyFrame, seed:Array<Float>, occurrence:String, connector:String, ?residualTolerance:Float):Null<Array<Float>>
fields.doc: Full socket orientation, including roll; the free-axis solver's existing tolerance is unchanged.

types.name: ArmAxis
types.doc: Direction of a joint axis, in the frame of the link that carries the joint.

types.name: ArmGripperTool
types.doc:
Pneumatic two-jaw tool for a cobot flange. The jaws and cylinder remain real
assembly members; the controller exposes one close command and the simulator
pulses the cylinder valve's two digital coil outputs.

types.name: ArmJoint
types.doc:
Joint module of a serial arm: a cylindrical housing along local +Z with a fixed `stator` face at
z=0 and the rotating output `rotor` face at z=length. The housing belongs to the link before the
joint; the next link mates its `start` connector to `rotor` on a revolute joint.

A module given a `flange` is the last joint of the arm. Its output carries the `RobotFlange`
plate against the housing end, so it has a `tool` connector at the flange's mounting face
instead of `rotor`: mate the flange's `face` to it, and a tool mates to the flange's pilot boss.
The recipe names the flange by its ISO 9409-1 pitch circle; 0 means no flange.

A module may carry a `servo`, the motor inside it: it is then a `MotorDrive`, and
`MachineAssembly.addMotor` puts its servo on the joint it turns, usually through a `Gearbox`.

fields.name: servo
fields.doc: The servo motor inside the module, or null when it is only a housing.

fields.name: componentType
fields.doc: Subclasses must declare their own recipe and saved values.

fields.name: actuator
fields.doc: The servo inside the module as an actuator on joint `joint`; a module with no servo is not a motor.

types.name: ArmLink
types.doc:
Hollow tube link of a serial arm along local +Z, closed at both ends, with a collar where it
meets the previous joint. Its `start` connector sits at the origin with the joint axis given by
`startAxis`; its `end` connector carries the next joint module, whose axis is `endAxis`. A
lateral end joint is centred on the tube's end point, so `end` is offset by half the module
length (`endJointLength`) against the axis direction.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (length:Float, diameter:Float, wall:Float, collarDiameter:Float, startAxis:ArmAxis, endAxis:ArmAxis, endJointLength:Float):Void

fields.name: axisToken
fields.doc: Recipe token for an axis: "+X", "-X" or "+Z".

fields.name: componentType
fields.doc: Subclasses must declare their own recipe and saved values.

types.name: ArmSuctionTool
types.doc:
Suction tool for the arm's ISO 9409-1 style tool flange: an adapter plate, a frame bar, and a
catalog ejector, cup, fitting and hose, arranged like the fixed EOAT in `examples/eoat`, with an
inline vacuum sensor between the ejector and the hose that tells a sealed cup from an open one.
Its `contact` working frame is the cup's contact face. The arm publishes `toolContact` and the
ejector's `compressedAir` inlet.

types.name: ArmTool
types.doc:
What the arm carries on its tool flange: the end effector built for that flange, and the
connectors and service inlets of it that the arm publishes as its own. The arm includes the
effector as `tool`, so `expose` names its members `tool/<member>`.

fields.name: expose
fields.doc: Publishes the tool's connectors and the service inlets that must be supplied from outside.

types.name: ArmWristFork
types.doc:
Clevis carried by j5, with the hand axis through the wrist centre.
The pitch module spans local X from -span/2 to +span/2. Its rotor mates to
start at +span/2; the next module sits on +Z, rather than inheriting the rotor
face's lateral offset. Dimensions are assumed engineering geometry in mm.

types.name: ChangerLockFacet
types.doc: A tool changer lock worked through `inletPort`.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: The facet of this kind on `component`, or null.

types.name: CobotArm
types.doc:
Offset six-axis arm assembled from source modules and the published class DH
geometry. Zero is the DH zero pose. The control hardware is offboard and is
excluded from the arm's stated mechanical mass.

fields.name: installToolService
fields.doc: Add the provisional wrist socket explicitly; existing arms retain their service layout.

fields.name: armMass
fields.doc: The moving mechanics and base plate, excluding offboard control hardware and a tool.

fields.name: holdingTorques
fields.doc:
Holding torque about each mechanical joint axis, including a point payload
at the flange. The assembly supplies every downstream mass and centre.
Values are signed N m; positions in the CAD state are millimetres.

fields.name: ready
fields.doc: A conventional elbow-down pose with a vertical tool axis.

types.name: CobotArmLink
types.doc:
Hollow, tapered bridge between parallel arm axes. A flat service land has
a separate cover; the uninterrupted lower shell carries the load. Cable ports
enter the bridge duct without claiming a through-bore in the drive modules.
Wall, boss and fastening dimensions are assumed construction.

fields.name: atService
fields.doc: Consume a solid in the service-cover frame.

types.name: CobotClass
types.doc: Size families of the offset six-axis cobot layout.

types.name: CobotJoint
types.doc:
An assumed strain-wave cobot module: housing, gearhead and
an integrated servo. The geometric pocket removes the installed gearhead's
volume from the housing. Output ratings describe the generic size family.

fields.name: driverCurrent
fields.doc: Assumed amplifier classes, with headroom above each module's phase RMS peak.

types.name: CobotLink
types.doc:
Tube and end caps between offset joint seats. The outgoing seat removes the
preceding housing's axial length from the DH transform; that length is already
present in its rotor face. The tube passes outside the housing radii.

types.name: CobotLinkCover
types.doc: Separate service lid or its nominal uncompressed NBR gasket. No ingress rating is implied.

types.name: CobotReference
types.doc:
UR e-series reference geometry. Mass includes the maker's stated cable allowance.
Sources: universal-robots.com/developer/hardware-and-motion/robot-motion-dh-parameters/
and the collective technical data sheet, November 2023. These describe size classes;
the generic module model does not claim to reproduce the manufacturer's internals.

types.name: CobotReferenceRow
types.doc:
Published DH dimensions (mm), payload (kg), and joint speeds (degrees/s).
Module construction and drive ratings are separate, assumed engineering values.

types.name: CobotToolLink
types.doc:
Rotating terminal housing between the sixth module and its tool flange.
Smooth, hollow, and tapered to the flange diameter, with a closed mounting
face at either end. Its extent accounts for the module and flange thickness
already present in the DH chain. It is assumed construction, not vendor CAD.

fields.name: radiusAt
fields.doc: Smoothstep gives a straight tangent at both ends of the taper.

types.name: CobotToolServiceMount
types.doc:
Prototype split collar following the generic terminal housing taper.
0.5 mm radial clearance reserves a liner; grip/preload and shell strength are unvalidated.

types.name: CobotToolServices
types.doc:
Optional electrical service provision for any generic CobotArm size class.
Input ports are controller-side boundaries. Bridges declare connectivity only:
no cable path through joints, rotary feedthrough, or unlimited wrist rotation is implied.

types.name: CobotWristLink
types.doc:
A hollow structural elbow between perpendicular wrist modules. The section is
sized from the modules, independently of the gap between them. A saddle relief
follows the next module's envelope; the inner cavity stops one wall before that
relief. Both DH mating planes stay fixed. Dimensions are assumed construction,
not a bearing or fatigue rating.

types.name: CobotWristMount
types.doc:
Assumed M4 wrist interface. A shallow annular locating shoulder stays outside
the installed gearhead; six holes share the remaining housing annulus. The
counterbore locates a structural hub, not a separately specified rolling bearing.

fields.name: housingCuts
fields.doc: In the joint's CAD frame; rotor is the +Z end, stator is z=0.

fields.name: rotorPocket
fields.doc:
Axisymmetric bearing/output recess in the fixed housing. The rotating
flange is a separate member; a bolt pattern must never be cut in a stator
and then expected to follow the driven joint.

fields.name: pilot
fields.doc: The mating hub's annular locating lip, in a frame pointing into the module.

types.name: CobotWristRotor
types.doc:
Assumed bearing-supported output flange, carried by the driven link. Its
annular skirt clears the installed gearhead. The bearing running clearance is
represented geometrically; this component does not specify rolling elements.

types.name: ConnectorFrame
types.doc: Millimetre frame whose connector approach axis is +Y.

types.name: DhDualGripperServices
types.doc:
Selected purchased harness for the two PGC-140-50 concept.
Expert provides an external-power entry; DH wiring compatibility and installation
remain unqualified. Selection is not a current rating or a collision certificate.

fields.name: addPurchases
fields.doc:
Inventory-only until a real installation pose/routing is defined.
Unknown mass intentionally avoids treating short illustrative CAD leads as stock mass.

types.name: DualArmGripperTool
types.doc: Two independently valved parallel grippers mounted at right angles on one wrist plate.

fields.name: INTER_GRIPPER_CLEARANCE_MM
fields.doc: Assumed free edge clearance between the two separately valved gripper envelopes.

fields.name: specB
fields.doc: B can handle a different commissioned part width from A.

fields.name: mountOffsetMm
fields.doc: Half-spacing of opposing stations on the adapter's tool bolt circle.

fields.name: adapterThicknessMm
fields.doc: Actual thickness of the flange adapter plate, including the assumed wrist stand-off.

fields.name: envelopeWidthMm
fields.doc: Conservative projected envelopes including the cylinder and routed air lines, in mm.

types.name: EndEffector
types.doc: One mountable end effector (EOAT), with mass and frames relative to its mount.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc: Own a stable builder snapshot when a changer accepts this tool.

fields.name: excludeFromCollision
fields.doc: Explicitly omit a member from generated collision geometry.

fields.name: mountReference
fields.doc: The connector that mates this unit to the robot or changer.

fields.name: mountTFrame
fields.doc: MachineKit frame in mm, relative to the robot-facing mount connector.

types.name: EndEffectorDescription
types.doc: An end effector as portable data: its assembly, and its mount and working frames.

types.name: EndEffectorFrames
types.doc: Frame conversions for end effector (EOAT) integration with RobotKit.

fields.name: pointYToZ
fields.doc: Coordinates in a +Y connector basis expressed in a +Z robot basis.

fields.name: approachYToZ
fields.doc: Change both connector-relative bases from MachineKit +Y to RobotKit +Z.

fields.name: toMetres
fields.doc: Convert a millimetre frame to metres with a plain position and quaternion.

types.name: EndEffectorPlate
types.doc:
Adapter plate between a robot's `RobotFlange` and a tool: one face mates to the flange's
mounting pattern (a blind recess for its pilot boss, bolt and pin clearance holes), the other
exposes its own bolt circle for a gripper or tool.

The default tool bolt circle lies outside the flange's bolt circle, far enough that tool and
flange screw heads clear each other; the plate grows past the flange diameter when needed to
carry it. A supplied tool bolt circle must keep every tool hole clear of the pilot recess, the
flange bolt and pin holes, and its neighbours.
CAD frame: robot-side face at z=0, tool-side face at z=thickness. Connectors: `robot` (the
flange mount, mate it to the flange's `face`), `tool` (the tool mount), and
`toolBolt1`..`toolBoltN`, all with +Y along +Z. The `robot` and `tool`
connectors point +X toward the flange's locating pin.

fields.name: toolBoltPattern
fields.doc: Tool-side bolt centres, counter-clockwise from angle 0.

types.name: EndEffectorSet
types.doc: Robot-side end effector (EOAT) stack with independently coupled tools.

fields.name: configuration
fields.doc: Build one coupled configuration, with no ports to other tools.

fields.name: configurationFromDescription
fields.doc: Evaluate a configuration from portable data without modifying the source description.

types.name: EndEffectorSetDescription
types.doc: A robot-side end effector with a tool changer, and the tools it can couple.

types.name: FairinoDualToolAdapter
types.doc:
Purchased complete adapter: connector bodies and leads are not separate BOM purchases.
Photo-based layout envelopes, NOT supplier dimensional CAD or verified electrical mating.
Standard is rigid; Expert includes illustrative straightened leads (not supplied lengths).
No electrical bridges are asserted until supplier wiring/backfeed behavior is documented.

types.name: FrameBar
types.doc: Simple rectangular robot tooling bar along local +Z.

fields.name: componentType
fields.doc: Subclasses must declare their own recipe and saved values.

types.name: GearedArmJoint
types.doc:
An arm housing machined for a separate gearbox member. The pocket is a physical dimension;
its clearance does not contribute mass a second time when the gearhead is installed.

types.name: GripFacet
types.doc: Gripper jaws with `strokeMm` of travel, opened and closed through two ports.

fields.name: forceN
fields.doc: Grip force in N, when known.

fields.name: graspSensor
fields.doc: Joint-switch id within the assembly that owns this gripper.

fields.name: contactConnector
fields.doc: Connector at the centre of the finger working zone.

fields.name: minimumPartWidthMm
fields.doc: Assumed blank-width range for which the physical jaw travel can close.

fields.name: fingerLengthMm
fields.doc: Usable finger length measured from the TCP toward the tool flange.

fields.name: fingerPadFrictionCoefficient
fields.doc: Assumed sliding friction coefficient of the replaceable finger pads.

fields.name: supportStep
fields.doc: Whether fingers have a physical support toe beneath the fingertip plane.

fields.name: padMembers
fields.doc: Contact members in the containing gripper assembly, declared by its design.

types.doc: Reference 6 mm service loops outside each gripper's -Y face.

types.name: IndustrialArmClass
types.doc: Generic spherical-wrist industrial arm reach classes. Geometry is assumed.

types.name: IndustrialArmReferenceRow
types.doc:
Assumed source-link dimensions in mm, not a manufacturer's specification.
These describe the mechanism; OPW parameters must be extracted from its
compiled joint axes rather than supplied from this table.

types.name: OffsetFingerGeometry
types.doc: Geometry for OffsetGripperFinger; coordinates are the shared closed-jaw interface frame.

fields.name: collisionBoxes
fields.doc: Construction bounds [x0,x1,y0,y1,z0,z1] before bores and the root-radius cut remove material.

types.name: OffsetFingerSpec
types.doc: Shared interface contract, independent of manufacturing route. Coordinates mm.

types.name: OffsetGripperFinger
types.doc: One functional part family; manufacturing variants own geometry and hardware.

fields.name: compressionSleeves
fields.doc: Owned sleeve solids; explicitly instantiate them in an assembly/BOM as hardware.

types.name: ParallelGripper
types.doc:
A complete, assumed double-acting pneumatic parallel gripper. One cylinder moves
the left jaw; the second jaw follows through a mirrored mechanical coupling.

types.name: ParallelGripperBody
types.doc:
Fixed housing and design interface for a two-jaw gripper. The complete
mechanism, moving jaws and pneumatic drive live in `ParallelGripper`.

types.name: ParallelGripperFinger
types.doc: Assumed replaceable contact pad sized for the bearing-block blank.

types.name: ParallelGripperJaw
types.doc:
One moving carriage. The second jaw uses the same part and the mirrored
prismatic coupling; its handed finger seat is derived from `side`.

types.name: ParallelGripperSpec
types.doc:
Assumed reference envelopes for two-jaw pneumatic grippers. Force is the
matched cylinder's extension force at 0.6 MPa; dimensions and speed are
generic catalogue values, not a vendor's verified row.

fields.name: HOUSING_SIDE_CLEARANCE
fields.doc: Assumed side clearance between the housing and the open-jaw envelope.

fields.name: GUIDE_TONGUE_REACH
fields.doc: Assumed carriage tongue running on the housing's relieved guide floor.

fields.name: CYLINDER_BRACKET_THICKNESS
fields.doc: Assumed side bracket plate thickness and attachment overlap on the housing.

fields.name: SWITCH_EDGE_CLEARANCE

base, for mounting a robot arm above a machine bed.

The column must be wider than the flange's bolt circle plus one screw head, so the top bolt
holes and heads stay on the column; it defaults to the flange diameter. The floor bolt circle
puts each floor screw head half a head diameter clear of the column, and the base extends half
a head diameter past the heads.

CAD frame: floor face at z=0, top mounting face at z=height. Connectors: `floor` and
`floorBolt1`/`anchor1` through `floorBoltN`/`anchorN` at the floor plane with +Y along +Z,
and `top` (the flange mount) at z=height with +Y along -Z, pointing into the pedestal like
every flange `Mount` connector. Mating the flange's `face` to `top` therefore turns the flange
over: its plate sits above the pedestal and its pilot boss drops into the top recess.

types.name: RobotFlange
types.doc:
Robot tool flange using the ISO 9409-1 bolt pattern: a round plate with a centring pilot, a bolt circle, and a
locating pin hole. The flange is sized by its pitch circle (`new RobotFlange(50)` is
based on the ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 pattern): pitch circle, bolt count and thread, pilot and pin diameters come from the
standard's table; the outer diameter (pitch circle plus two screw-head diameters), plate
thickness (1.5 screw diameters), and pilot height (half a screw diameter) are proportional. The
pilot is modelled as a raised boss that engages a recess in the mating part (ISO specifies the
robot side's d2/d3 centring feature as a recess; this preview intentionally uses a raised pilot
for a simpler mate, so its designation says ISO style rather than exact ISO interface.
Passing a `boltCount` that differs from the table gives a non-standard pattern whose
designation drops the ISO pattern prefix.

CAD frame: mounting face at z=0, flange plate behind it (z=-thickness..0), pilot boss toward +Z
(z=0..pilotHeight). Connectors: `face` (the mounting face), `bolt1`..`boltN` and `pin`, all at
z=0 with +Y along +Z, pointing out of the face into the mated part. The `face` connector's
+X points toward the locating pin. A mated part's `Mount`
connector follows the same rule, so `mate(flange.face, part.mount)` stacks the part in front of
the face; `mountingCutout` is the matching tool in that part's frame.

overshoots the mating face by 0.1, and the holes overshoot `depth` by 0.1, so no cut face is
coplanar with the part's faces.

types.name: LinearDriveSizing
types.doc:
Preliminary conservative envelope, not a supplier thermal/torque-speed qualification.
Duty: full-stroke loaded out-and-back, acceleration/cruise/deceleration and one second dwell.
Force magnitudes add cutting, gravity, drag and inertia in either direction, never cancel.
External rotary inertia receives a conservative efficiency penalty, even where
some of it sits at the reducer input. The motor rotor itself receives none.
Continuous screening also checks indefinite cutting at the requested rapid speed.

A small bracket made of rectangular blocks square to its own frame, welded or machined into one part: what holds a
switch or a sensor off the member it is bolted to. Its blocks are given in its own frame.

types.name: BracketBlock
types.doc: One block of a `BlockBracket`: its corners in the bracket's own frame, millimetres.

types.name: CastInsert
types.doc: Cast-in steel design envelope; local +Z is the finished mounting-plane normal.

fields.name: manufacturedValues
fields.doc:
Grade and the attached manufacturing choices are authored together, so a
recipe rebuild never depends on whether defaults were resolved beforehand.

fields.name: precastHoles
fields.doc:
Explicit source authoring for holes which must exist during the pour.
Bought-part mounting holes use their separate connector/clearance-budget route.

fields.name: insertSpec
fields.doc: Complete source design; the published physical facet follows buildStage.

types.name: CastingCavityCad
types.doc:
Native realization of the authoritative derived region, including exact
cut/body expressions. This is the shared CAD backend, not local cut clipping.

types.name: CastingCollisionQualification
types.doc: Explicit qualification of the exact collision model, separate from CAD availability.

types.name: CastingFeaturePatterns
types.doc: Shared source patterns; constants and ownership belong to the caller.
