types.name: CastingProfileCad
types.doc: Shared exact source/panel boundary. Drawings use these same line/arc records.

types.name: CastingRegionCad
types.doc:
Native evaluation of neutral finished-region expressions. All temporaries
close on success and failure; zero-volume contacts are not solid material.

types.name: CastingSolids
types.doc:
Source and tooling realize the same neutral exterior in the insert frame.
These are solid exteriors; drilling is applied separately from source holes.

types.name: Channel
types.doc:
C-section channel, extruded along local +Z from z=0 to z=`length`. The web sits at local
x=0..thickness spanning the full `height`; the flanges open toward +X.

types.name: CutListLine
types.doc:
Lengths of one profile aggregated across every member that uses it. `totalLength` sums the
members' cut lengths after their explicit end setbacks.

types.name: DrawingExtrusionProfile
types.doc:
Extrudes an explicit drawing section at any length, retaining line, bulge-arc and circle geometry.
Input loops are canonical XY: outer counterclockwise, holes clockwise, no inferred slot dimensions.

fields.name: sectionText
fields.doc: Geometry only, embedded in recipe assemblies; no download paths or supplier metadata.

types.name: EmbeddedAnchorCad
types.doc: Exact occupied volumes of real standard hardware, in casting coordinates.

types.name: FixingSockets
types.doc: Catalogue variants create the ordinary insert component, not another component family.

fields.name: LENGTH
fields.doc:
PFEIFER fixing socket, crimped end: M6 x 40, a=25, e=6; grade 1.4571.
Catalogue concrete capacity is not mineral-cast anchorage evidence.

fields.name: TIP_GAP_PITCHES
fields.doc:
In-house study rules: one pitch at the blind bottom; >=0.8 mm sleeve
ligament and >=0.5 mm closed-end material to avoid a resin path. They screen
geometry only, not strength. The unverified exterior cannot qualify them.

fields.name: FEATURE_SEPARATION_DIAMETERS
fields.doc: In-house machining separation, independently of ISO 273 bolt clearance.

types.name: FlatBar
types.doc:
Solid rectangular bar, extruded along local +Z from z=0 to z=`length`, cross-section centred
on the axis.

types.name: FootStemEnvelope
types.doc: Nominal right-hand metric foot hardware. These dimensions do not qualify a load rating.

types.name: FoundationIntegrity
types.doc: Geometry/tolerance checks only. No structural, modal or process adequacy claim.

fields.name: castingReview
fields.doc:
Source-bound level-1 casting checks enter the same design Diagnostics.
Capture context independently from the owning assembly, not the document.
Standalone foundations can omit it.

fields.name: checkMounts
fields.doc: Named steel supports; a supplied connection map also checks the actual assembly mates.

fields.name: analysisMembers
fields.doc: Copies of authored centreline data; does not expose mutable frame internals.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: Straight-line distance between the frame nodes on a member's centreline.

fields.name: cutLength
fields.doc: Stock length between the mitre long points; square and coped ends remain node-to-node.

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc: The member's `Part` placed in world space along its endpoints and extended to mitre long points.

fields.name: cutList
fields.doc: Cut lengths aggregated by profile designation, in first-used order.

types.name: FrameEndCut
types.doc:
End treatment for one structural member. A mitre's `setback` is the axial difference between
the short and long points across the section; its plane passes through the frame node. The long
point is on local -X at either end. A cope's
`setback` is the radius of a cylindrical tool whose axis follows the mating member through the
shared node.

types.name: FrameMember
types.doc:
Builds a structural frame from named 3D points and members that extrude a `StructuralProfile`
between two points. A frame is one rigid weldment, not a kinematic mechanism, so members carry
no assembly joints: `geometry(name)` returns the member's `Part` already placed in world space.

Members are placed by their centreline nodes. Square and coped members keep node-to-node stock;
mitre planes pass through the nodes and add stock to reach the long points. `length` is the
node-to-node distance, while `cutLength` and `cutList` report stock lengths including mitres.

Section orientation: the profile's local +Z runs from `start` to `end`, its local +Y (a
channel's `height`, an angle's `legB`, a tube's `height`) follows `reference` projected
perpendicular to the member's axis, and its local +X is +Y x +Z. `reference` defaults to +Z,
or +Y when the member is nearly vertical, matching the axis-picking convention CadKit's own
examples use for arbitrary-direction placement; a `reference` parallel to the member is an
error.

types.name: FrameSeat
types.doc: A place the frame's design gives a part that mounts on it: a connector frame in the frame's coordinates, its +Z out of the frame.

types.name: FrameWeld
types.doc: Two members welded together, with the fillet leg in millimetres.

types.name: InsertAnchorHardware
types.doc:
Standard components are the dimension authority. Source choices reference
holes already declared by InsertHoles; no anchor hole is invented here.

fields.name: backPattern
fields.doc:
Source authoring: add only the declared back-hole pattern. Existing bought-part
hole routes remain unchanged, including transfer drilling after casting.

fields.name: minimumBandDepth
fields.doc:
Minimum pad depth around a central access opening. Both anchor bands use
the same smallest stock-compatible thread and edge/cover rule as derive.

fields.name: minimumOuterLand
fields.doc: Extra resin land beyond a steel plate edge for its outermost anchor.

types.name: InsertAnchorPatternRule
types.doc:
One source design rule, shared by every insert in a machine recipe. All
lengths are derived from the chosen standard thread or the back footprint.

types.name: InsertBodies
types.doc: Realize insert-only retention geometry separately from design-cut primitives.

types.name: InsertGeometry
types.doc:
Source and tooling realize the same neutral insert, without inventing a
component role, material or label to reconstruct contact geometry.

types.name: InsertHoles
types.doc: Recipe patterns regenerate the authoritative DesignInterfaces facet.

fields.name: tappedBlind
fields.doc:
Flat-bottom blind bore (flat-bottom drill or end mill), followed by tapping.
Cylindrical depth includes the tip gap and bottoming-tap runout; back wall is
checked against the actual insert thickness before a recipe is emitted.

types.name: InsertMountPattern
types.doc:
Source authoring only. Mounting positions come from placed component
connectors; the one stored hole frame is the intersection with finished steel.

types.name: LevelingFoot
types.doc:
Shared nominal foot hardware: bought foot, pad, screw, removable plate or nut.
Saved dimensions are layout assumptions. Supplier geometry and load qualification remain pending.

types.name: LevelingFootCodec
types.doc: One strict saved representation; previous machine-specific foot recipes are not read.

types.name: LevelingFootSpec
types.doc:
A complete purchased foot remains one BOM item; loose plates and nuts are separate items.
All local solids start at Z=0. Foot mountHeight is an assembly datum, not stem length.

fields.name: Foot
fields.signature: (padDiameter:Float, padHeight:Float, thread:ThreadSpec, stemBottom:Float, stemTop:Float, mountHeight:Float, envelope:FootStemEnvelope, collar:FootCollar)

types.name: MineralCasting
types.doc: Source design cuts and openings; finished cavities have one neutral derivation.

types.name: MineralFoundation
types.doc:
A casting and its separately itemised steel inserts, with matching recesses.
Layouts belong to the machine using this assembly, not to the component core.

types.name: PlateSeat
types.doc: Where something mounts on a plate: a connector frame and the through-holes it bolts through, in plate coordinates.

types.name: ProfileMember
types.doc: Cut structural stock along local +Z. Hollow sections retain their actual material and mass.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc: Cut stock lies along its length (+Z), whatever the cut.

fields.name: tslotRecipeType
fields.doc: Shared modular T-slot members, optionally carrying a complete measured section variant.

fields.name: drawingRecipeType
fields.doc: Section-defined members such as slotted plates; exact lines/arcs/holes travel with the assembly.

types.name: RectTube
types.doc:
Rectangular (or, with `width == height`, square) hollow structural tube, extruded along
local +Z from z=0 to z=`length`, cross-section centred on the axis.

types.name: RectTubeMember
types.doc: A cut rectangular tube with end mounting frames; dimensions are in millimetres.

types.name: RoundTube
types.doc: Round hollow structural tube, extruded along local +Z from z=0 to z=`length`.

types.name: SeatedPlate
types.doc:
A flat plate lying on its base (z = 0), centred on its origin. It owns the layout of what mounts on it: each seat is a
connector and the holes for its fasteners, so moving a seat moves both, and a part mounted on a seat sits where the seat
says (its own connector mated to the seat), never the other way round. Slots (centre x, centre y, length along X,
width along Y) are cut clean through.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (length:Float, width:Float, thickness:Float, name:String, seats:Array<PlateSeat>, ?slots:Array<{x:Float, y:Float, length:Float, width:Float}>, ?material:String):Void

fields.name: onTop
fields.doc: Seat frame on the top face at (x, y), facing up.

fields.name: underneath
fields.doc: Seat frame on the underside at (x, y), facing up like the parts hung from it.

types.name: SlideInSlotNut
types.doc:
Dimension-driven end-loaded nut. XY is the bearing plane; ridge top Z=0,
shoulders Z=-ridgeHeight and bottom Z=-height. X is across the slot.
Sharp corners conservatively retain unspecified chamfers. Threads are semantic.
A series name alone never establishes a fit or a load rating.

fields.name: fitEnvelope
fields.doc: Unperforated conservative envelope for interference checks. Caller owns it.

types.name: SocketExteriorStudy
types.doc: Undimensioned exterior choices belong to the source setup, never the supplier data.

types.name: StructuralProfile
types.doc:
A cross-section factory for `FrameAssembly` members: `geometry(length)` extrudes the section
along local +Z from z=0 to z=length, matching every other machinekit generator's axis
convention. `RectTube`, `RoundTube`, `Angle`, `Channel`, and `FlatBar` implement this.

types.name: TSlotExtrusion
types.doc:
T-slot aluminium extrusion profile. The numeric constructor remains a generic proportional
approximation; `forProfile()` selects a catalog-backed profile with vendor dimensions.

fields.name: systemId
fields.doc: Shared dimensional system; does not assert cross-vendor hardware qualification.

fields.name: forSystem
fields.doc:
Supplier-neutral slot-8 layout candidates. Preview slot/bore dimensions are approximate;
use a measured section variant when internal shape matters. Existing catalog rows are unchanged.

fields.name: drawingSection
fields.doc: Portable detailed sections use a self-contained geometry recipe, never a local supplier path.

fields.name: catalog
fields.doc: MISUMI HFS5 profile catalog, with nominal cross-section dimensions in millimetres.

fields.name: forProfile
fields.doc: Construct a catalog-backed profile by designation, for example `HFS5-2040`.

fields.name: nominalGeometry
fields.doc: Simplified shared layout; source section variants retain their own cavities and curved details.

fields.name: modeledSlotDepth
fields.doc:
Depth actually removed by geometry(), including its corner-web allowance. Hardware fit
must use this value rather than the nominal catalog slotDepth. Faces rotate from +X.

types.name: TSlotProfileSpec
types.doc:
Catalog dimensions for a vendor extrusion profile. Slot dimensions are in the cross-section;
the profile is extruded along local +Z from z=0 to z=`length`.

types.name: TSlotTable
types.doc:
Floor-standing, square-profile extrusion table. Dimensions are mm, top height includes feet
and worktop. Front inset moves the entire front support row toward the back. Connections are derived from an explicit
hardware specification; optional rear bracing is selected by the caller, not load-rated.

fields.name: partPath
fields.doc: Resolve a manufacturing member name to its stable assembly occurrence path.

fields.name: footAdjustment
fields.doc:
Available extension about the nominal pose, limited by the drilled bore and 1.5D engagement.
Changing an assembled foot extension also changes that corner's top height.

fields.name: collisionPieces
fields.doc: Conservative individual envelopes; slot cavities and foot-pad corners are filled.

types.name: TSlotTableFootprint
types.doc:
Outer dimensions of the low base rails. Offsets are relative to the top's centre.
The footprint must contain the entire upper frame; extra depth/width can be asymmetric.

types.name: TSlotTableHardware
types.doc:
Nominal dimensional hardware specification, not a supplier SKU or load rating.
Nuts are end-loaded rectangular slot plates: insert before closing the frame.
Threads are semantic, consistent with MachineKit's standard fasteners.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (boltSize:String, bracketThickness:Float, nutWidth:Float, nutLength:Float, nutThickness:Float, footThread:String, footEngagement:Float):Void

fields.name: nutDepth
fields.doc: Installed nut bears against the slot retaining lip; clearance remains behind it.

fields.name: bracketScrewLength
fields.doc: Select a stocked nominal length; reject instead of silently using a special-length bolt.

types.name: TSlotTableParts
types.doc: Shared primitives for the generator; all sizes are mm.

types.name: TableAngle
types.doc: Local X extends away from the leg, Z=0 touches the rail underside.

types.name: TableFootPlate
types.doc:
Foot adapter below a horizontal base rail. Central tapped foot bore and two recessed
slot screws avoid trying to tap the open extrusion slot for a vertical levelling stem.

types.name: TableRearBrace
types.doc: Rear strap: local Y joins the hole centres; Z points outward from the table.

types.name: TableSlotNut
types.doc: An end-loaded plate nut occupies only the undercut, not the slot throat.

types.name: WeldedFrame
types.doc:
A welded structural frame: members of a `FrameAssembly` cut and welded into one rigid part, in the frame's own
coordinates, carrying the seats its design gives the parts that mount on it. A weldment is one body, so it is one
member of a machine, not a tree of tubes pretending to hold each other up.

Its geometry is the members' union and its stock `cutList()`. Its welds are declared, and `seams()` finds each one in
the members' geometry (`Weldment`), so a weld declared between members that do not meet is reported, not drawn.

fields.name: weldment
fields.doc: The welds as a `Weldment` of the frame's members, its first member the reference.

fields.name: seams
fields.doc: The seams of every declared weld, found in the members' geometry, in the frame's coordinates.

fields.name: memberBounds
fields.doc: The box of member `name`, in the frame's coordinates: the part of the frame something is bolted to.

types.name: AssemblyFemExport
types.doc: Study-independent posed bodies. Callers own selections, interfaces and solver assumptions.

fields.name: stepText
fields.doc: Preserve geometry while stabilizing timestamps and OCCT's Product N labels.

fields.name: bodies
fields.signature: (assembly:MachineAssembly, state:AssemblyState, folder:String, exportSolid:(String) -> Bool):{parts:Array<Dynamic>, materials:Array<Dynamic>, totalMassKg:Float, solidMassKg:Float}

types.name: BoxMoldCad
CastingFillAnalysis
types.doc:
The native BREP backend of the shared flat-free-surface process model.
Input parts are borrowed. Pocket geometry names an exact source component,
never a box approximation. Additional output levels cannot affect trap IDs.

fields.name: fromPlan
fields.doc: Bridge actual source and actual mold members into the one process pipeline.

types.name: CastingFillGeometry
types.doc:
Native geometry backend for the existing critical-level fill analysis.
Bounds size the clipping tools only. Every returned region, section and volume
is an exact BREP Boolean; neither voxels nor sampled levels are introduced.
The caller owns returned parts and closes this backend independently.

fields.name: heightInterval
fields.doc:
Exact global height interval. Bounds only place enclosing planes; native
shape distance determines the actual extrema, including curved edges.

fields.name: criticalHeights
fields.doc:
The complete height extrema of each conic/straight boundary edge, plus
its vertices. Finite planes enclose the whole XY projection, so exact
shape distance measures height rather than a distance to a plane edge.
Higher-order boundary curves need a stationary-point solver; never use
their bounds as a claimed critical level.

fields.name: airComponents
fields.doc:
Boolean solids preserve positive-area connectivity. A mere point or edge
at an event plane cannot join two air volumes into one solid.

fields.name: componentKey
fields.doc:
Geometry identity within one fingerprinted source/level. A duplicate key
among disconnected components is rejected by the fill analysis rather
than resolved by native topology order. Rounding is for identity only.

fields.name: projectedOpening
fields.doc:
Project all tooling at/above the fill plane, including a contacting face.
The existing exact swept-volume construction supplies the projection.

fields.name: ceilingWidths
fields.doc:
Conservative projected widths of potential ceiling patches. Refinement
joins same-domain faces before measuring, so Boolean seams cannot turn a
broad roof into apparently narrow strips. A non-axial curved face uses
its full projected width; it may overestimate its upward-facing portion.

types.name: CastingMoldCad
types.doc: CAD bridge for neutral multi-core box plans. Frames and exact operations remain authoritative.

fields.name: plan
fields.doc:
Native planning entry point; pure ManufacturingKit callers can retain
the exact box algebra or supply a different exact kernel explicitly.

fields.name: decode
fields.doc: Restore non-box plans without relying on a preceding planning call.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Real source resin, including the exact standard anchor occupancy.

types.name: CastingMoldExport
types.doc: Review outputs only. Existing CadKit writers render the exact panel operations.

types.name: CastingSectionContours
types.doc:
Exact BREP sections in the declared plane's XY coordinates, shared by
drawings and machining. Only straight/circular boundaries become line/arc
records; unsupported curves and ambiguous junctions never become polygons.

fields.name: normalFrame
fields.doc: Right-handed section frame with local Z along a declared unit normal.

types.name: FoundationAssemblyContext
types.doc:
Explicit instance bindings preserve source ownership across assembly nesting.
This copies declared interface/axis facts, not casting strategies or tolerances.

types.name: FoundationJointCad
types.doc:
Finite tip-bearing coverage from actual source components. This checks nominal
contact only: stability, strength, tightening and measured fit remain separate.

fields.name: contacts
fields.signature: (source:FoundationJointSources, joint:FoundationJoint, local:(String) -> Part, pose:(String) -> AssemblyFrame):Array<{id:String, report:PlanarContactCad.PlanarCoverage}>

fields.name: review
fields.doc: Reconstruct only standard/source geometry recorded in the fingerprint.

types.name: FoundationToolingAdapter
types.doc: Detached copy of source design records and the authoritative hole facet.

types.name: InsertAnchorGeometry
types.doc:
Native checks of source hardware. Strength, locking evidence and tooling
interference remain separate; source shape bounds never substitute for solids.

fields.name: reviewMold
fields.doc:
Actual source hardware against every realized tooling member. The insert's
own threaded engagement and its own screw/washer contact are intentional.

types.name: InsertDrawing
types.doc:
Nominal orthographic body views and source hole-entry projections, not CAM
contours. The hole schedule retains entry frames, depth, thread and route.
CadKit's existing exporters render the same Drawing2D in both formats.

types.name: InsertFixtureCad
types.doc: Shared CAD realization of a source-hole carrier: all steel comes from the source input.

fields.name: check
fields.doc:
Exact removal graph after the explicitly required unscrewing operations.
Insert/casting solids are stationary obstacles; only tooling is swept.

fields.name: assembly
fields.doc: Explicit fastener release precedes the translation checks; the insert stays in the casting.

types.name: MoldPlayback
types.doc: Static snapshots of checked steps, never a new motion/adhesion/flip simulation.

fields.name: scene
fields.doc:
Static presentation scenes have no collision proxies or dynamics. Exact validation
lives in the fingerprint-bound CAD review, not approximate viewer boxes.

types.name: NativeCastingMoldKernel
types.doc:
Exact CAD queries used by non-box planning. Caches retain numbers only;
every native resource closes before a query returns, including throw paths.

types.name: NativeFillPart
types.doc:
Boundary owners supplement the globally unique member ID. Anchor IDs are
local to their insert, so both source IDs accompany the hardware member.

types.name: PanelCad
types.doc: Exact neutral-to-CadKit conversion shared by solid realization and drawings.

types.name: PanelDrawing
types.doc: Rendering stays in MachineKit; existing CadKit SVG/DXF writers consume Drawing2D.

fields.name: checkToolAccess
fields.doc: Borrowed free-approach tool envelopes; contact/engagement belongs outside them.

types.name: PlanarContactCad
types.doc:
Exact nominal planar face coverage, with the real boundaries and holes.
A volume section through an interior plane is not a boundary contact.
Physical hardware, alignment evidence and replication chemistry stay separate.

types.name: ReplicationContactCad
types.doc: Native replication qualification uses the shared finite boundary checker.

types.name: SocketFixtureCad
types.doc: Coupon review walls around the common source-insert fixture; no socket specification is duplicated here.

fields.name: cavity
fields.doc: This review enclosure deliberately accepts one exact rectangular casting envelope.

fields.name: presentation
fields.doc: Views refer to the single engineering assembly, in its length unit.

types.name: SweptRemoval
types.doc:
Exact straight-translation sweeps. Inputs remain borrowed; every temporary is closed.
Planar/cylindrical faces and axial or transverse conical withdrawals are supported. Other surfaces fail explicitly.

fields.name: analyze
fields.doc: Full-set diagonal clears every possible projected bound along a unit direction.

types.name: ToolingBlock
types.doc:
Rebuildable block in stock coordinates [0,w] x [0,d] x [0,h].
Visual material is explicit; supplier/process evidence remains in CorePlan.

types.name: ToolingDiagnostics
types.doc: Use the same code/subject/severity vocabulary as machinekit.design.

types.name: ToolingExplode
types.doc: Converts producer review displacements to the presentation's parent-frame coordinates.

types.name: ToolingFabricationExport
types.doc: Lists and shop-review drawings from neutral records. No alternative SVG/DXF writers.

types.name: ToolingFastenerFit
types.doc:
Nominal geometric engagement from the actual selected components. This does
not establish tightening, strip strength, load capacity or physical evidence.

fields.name: nutOverlap
fields.doc:
Exact coaxial interval overlap, using the screw's full threaded length
measured from its tip. Nut CAD runs from local Z=0 to Z=height; screw CAD
runs toward -Z from its head bearing face. Reversed nut placement is valid.

fields.name: requireNut
fields.doc:
Require the entire nominal nut thickness to be on full screw thread.
This deliberately does not use the insert-steel engagement policy: the
selected standard nut is a different component and its strength is separate.

types.name: ToolingFiles
types.doc: Generated output trees also work in fresh checkouts with no prior tooling build.

types.name: ToolingHardwareCad
types.doc: Nominal metric stack from the plan's selected screw diameter.

fields.name: fixtureScrew
fields.doc:
A nominal study screw into a real source hole. Length excludes its washer.
Validate the actual standard component before mutating the assembly.

types.name: ToolingInsertCad
types.doc: A copy back into the common source component: no inferred holes, roles or dimensions.

types.name: ToolingPackageManifest
types.doc: Deterministic inventory of a freshly generated directory, excluding this manifest itself.

types.name: ToolingPanel
types.doc: Rebuildable exact panel; material is an explicit CAD/BOM material selection.

types.name: ToolingPin
types.doc: Nominal locating pins and stepped bore masks; supplier fits need qualification.

fields.name: boreSeat
fields.doc:
A bore mask's frame in its hole's frame (z = 0 at the entry, +z into the bore): a pin already runs along
+z; a threaded mask is a set screw, which is turned so its socket stays at the entry.

types.name: ToolingPresentation
types.doc: Adapts planner order and world withdrawal directions; the viewer never sorts the steps.

types.name: ToolingProcessExport
types.doc: Neutral process results enter the same fabrication manifest/readiness gate.

types.name: ToolingSectionDrawing
types.doc:
Nominal section sheets from actual finished tooling, without stock-bound
silhouettes or cutter compensation. Existing CadKit exporters own text output.

fields.name: byDirection
fields.doc:
Reference sections along a declared removal direction. Actual extrema,
not bounding-box faces, determine the end sections.

types.name: ToolingSectionReview
types.doc: Finished-tooling drawing evidence, separate from machining and physical fit.

types.name: ToolingSourceCasting
types.doc: A detached casting source, with one strict neutral encoding and exact cavities.

types.name: ToolingVolume
types.doc: Rebuildable exact finished tooling volume, in mold coordinates (mm).

fields.name: fromCoreCutting
fields.doc:
Realize finished foam, never the rectangular cutting blank. Placement is
the record's stockToMold frame, supplied by the assembly caller.

types.name: BeltElasticity
types.doc: Compile one shaft belt's physical spans, regardless of how many motion records refer to it.

fields.name: rotaryJoint
fields.doc: Follow rigid attachments to the rotary shaft carrying this pulley.

types.name: BeltPair
types.doc: What a belt is made of when it runs round two pulleys of one belt family, which a recipe can rebuild.

types.name: BeltPoint
types.doc: A point on the belt's pitch line in its plane, and the direction the belt travels through it.

types.name: BeltPoseContext
types.doc: One uncoupled, unbounded pose copy shared by pose-dependent transmissions in a rebuild.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Every source starts at the same authored zero pose.

types.name: BeltStrand
types.doc: A straight run of the belt between two wraps: where it leaves one and meets the next.

fields.name: dx
fields.doc: Unit direction of travel, from the start to the end.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (from:Int, to:Int, startX:Float, startY:Float, endX:Float, endY:Float, dx:Float, dy:Float, length:Float):Void

types.name: BeltStretch
types.doc: Elastic energy in the two paths from an attached clamp to the held driving pulley.

fields.name: reduction
fields.signature: (belt:TimingBelt, path:BeltPathRecord, leader:String, follower:String, driver:String, driven:String, mechanical:AssemblyDefinition, relation:TransmissionRelation, ?context:BeltPoseContext):Float
fields.doc: Two loaded pulley attachments, with every intermediate wrap free to turn.

fields.name: contactDirection
fields.doc: Relative pulley direction about the belt normal, from its physical contact sides.

fields.name: spanStiffness
fields.doc: Axial spring of one free belt span, shared by clamp and rotary drives.

fields.name: law
fields.doc: Exact affine span geometry for straight Cartesian clamp travel. Unsupported changing wrap geometry is refused.

fields.name: axisSign
fields.doc: Positive joint rotation as seen about the belt-plane normal.

fields.name: stiffness
fields.doc: Certified weakest stiffness over the declared travel, from the same law used by physics.

types.name: BeltWrap
types.doc:
A pulley or idler a belt runs around, in the belt's plane: its pitch-circle centre and radius,
and the way the belt wraps it. `side` is +1 when the belt wraps it counter-clockwise (as seen
from the plane's +Z) and -1 when it wraps it clockwise, as it does an idler pressing on the
belt's outside.

types.name: GearPair
types.doc:
Two spur gears meshed at their profile-shifted centre distance, both rotating about parallel
+Z axes. `a` sits at the origin; `pose` places `b` along `a`'s local +X, turned about its own
axis so the teeth interleave.

fields.name: DEFAULT_EFFICIENCY
fields.doc: Assumed power efficiency of a single lubricated spur mesh.

fields.name: operatingPressureAngle
fields.doc: Derived operating pressure angle after the profile-shift centre-distance change.

fields.name: backlash
fields.doc: Sum of the two gears' tangential backlash allowances.

fields.name: profileShiftSum
fields.doc: Sum of the two gears' profile-shift coefficients.

fields.name: bRotation
fields.doc: Rotation of `b` about its +Z axis, radians, in `0 <= angle < 2*pi/b.teeth`.

fields.name: relation
fields.doc: Resolve the coupling from these parts.

fields.name: ratio
fields.doc: Gear ratio, driven teeth over driving teeth: `b.teeth / a.teeth`.

fields.name: pose
fields.doc:
World pose for `b` when `a` sits at the identity pose: translated to the centre distance
and turned by `bRotation` about +Z.

types.name: HelicalPinion
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class normal-module helical pinion. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: axialThrust
fields.doc: Signed axial force for a signed tangential force; bearing reactions oppose this.

fields.name: transverseContactRatio
fields.doc: Transverse pinion/rack contact ratio for unshifted full-depth teeth.

types.name: HelicalRack
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class normal-module helical rack. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc: Lies along its length (+Z) with its teeth (+Y) up.

fields.name: relation
fields.doc: rad/mm for pinion rotation driven by rack travel, matching Rack.relation.

types.name: PackedTimingBeltMesh
types.doc: Reusable display mesh storage. SceneKit copies these streams when publishing geometry.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Same tooth profile and face winding as TimingBeltMesh, without per-tooth temporary arrays.

types.name: PreloadedPinionMount
types.doc:
Assumed catalogue-class hinged spring-preloaded pinion mount. Dimensions mm; SI ratings unless stated.
Geometry is a nominal layout envelope, not manufacturing or supplier geometry.

fields.name: preload
fields.doc: N at the pinion for spring extension measured in mm.

types.name: Rack
types.doc:
Involute rack: the straight-flank limit of a spur gear's tooth profile (infinite pitch
radius), for meshing with a `SpurGear` of the same module and pressure angle.

CAD frame: pitch line at y=0, teeth pointing toward +Y, length along local +Z from z=0 to
z=length (a tooth gap centred at each end, so the root line runs out to square end faces),
extruded along local +X for `faceWidth`.

fields.name: DEFAULT_EFFICIENCY
fields.doc: Assumed power efficiency of a lubricated rack and pinion.

fields.name: backlash
fields.doc: Tangential reversal clearance at the pitch line, mm.

fields.name: presentationView
fields.doc: Lies along its length (+Z) with its teeth (+Y) up.

fields.name: relation
fields.doc: Resolve the coupling from these parts.

types.name: RackGeometry
types.doc: The pitch geometry shared by straight and normal-module helical rack drives.

types.name: RollerChainSource
types.doc: A chain member states the pitch and roller size that its sprockets must accept.

types.name: RollerChainSpec
types.doc: Nominal ANSI single-strand roller chain pitch and roller diameter, millimetres.

types.name: ScrewStretch
types.doc: Axial load path from the nut's physical bore to the actual fixed bearing, not the bending support or full shaft length.

types.name: Sprocket
types.doc:
Roller chain sprocket with a simplified tooth outline (straight flanks between root and tip
radii, not the true ANSI B29.1 seating-curve profile), extruded along local +Z.
Diameters follow the standard relations: pitch diameter p / sin(pi/z), root (seating) diameter
pitch diameter minus the roller diameter, outside diameter p * (0.6 + cot(pi/z)). The roller
generic constructor defaults roller diameter to 0.625 p; `forChain` uses tabulated
nominal pitch and roller diameter from a specific ANSI chain family.
CAD frame: front face at z=0, back face at z=thickness, matching `DeepGrooveBearing`.
Connectors: `front`, `back` (faces) and `axis` (mid-thickness), all with +Y along +Z.

fields.name: DEFAULT_EFFICIENCY
fields.doc: Assumed chain efficiency and bearing drag; chain stretch and chordal variation are not modelled.

fields.name: relation
fields.doc: Resolve the coupling from these parts.

types.name: SpurGear
types.doc:
External involute spur gear, full-depth teeth (addendum and dedendum are adjusted by the
profile-shift coefficient), extruded along local +Z from z=0 to z=faceWidth. Backlash is a
tangential allowance at the pitch circle and reduces the generated tooth thickness.

Tooth flanks are sampled points along the true involute-of-a-circle curve, not exact curves;
that is enough fidelity to mesh visually while keeping the outline a single closed polygon.
Below the base circle the flank drops to the root circle on a straight radial step rather
than a fillet. Tooth counts whose selected profile shift still requires undercut are rejected.

fields.name: MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE
fields.doc: Accepted pressure-angle range, 14.5 to 25 degrees: the standard involute systems.

fields.name: profileShift
fields.doc: Profile-shift coefficient x, in module units.

fields.name: backlash
fields.doc: Tangential backlash allowance at the pitch circle, in millimetres.

fields.name: boreDiameter
fields.doc: Shaft bore diameter; zero leaves the original solid gear blank.

fields.name: minimumUnshiftedTeeth
fields.doc: Conservative no-undercut full-depth limit: ceil(2 / sin(pressureAngle)^2).

fields.name: minimumProfileShift
fields.doc: Conservative minimum profile shift coefficient for a full-depth gear with this tooth count.

fields.name: validPressureAngle
fields.doc: True for pressure angles within `MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE`..`MAX_PRESSURE_ANGLE` (radians).

fields.name: centerDistance
fields.doc:
Centre distance to mesh with `other`, including the sum of both profile shifts. Both gears
must share a module and pressure angle. Backlash changes tooth thickness, not centre distance.

fields.name: pitchToothThickness
fields.doc: Tooth thickness measured along the pitch circle after profile shift and backlash.

types.name: TimingBelt
types.doc:
A closed timing belt running around pulleys and idlers given in a plane. The loop is the
pitch line: straight strands tangent to the wraps and arcs on them, in the order the wraps are
given. Its length divided by the pitch is the tooth count a belt of that length has.

The component's frame is the belt's plane, X and Y, with the belt `width` along +Z from 0.
Geometry is the belt's band, `thickness` thick and centred on the pitch line, as a straight
sided polygon; it has no teeth, since the band alone sweeps cheaply and the teeth would not
change any clearance.

`loop` lists the wraps in the order the belt visits them. The belt must not cross itself.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: Length of the pitch line, in millimetres.

fields.name: teeth
fields.doc: The whole number of teeth nearest the length: what a belt built for it has.

fields.name: statedCordRigidity
fields.doc: Explicit assumed cord EA per mm of belt width, N; zero selects recorded family data.

fields.name: statedDampingRatio
fields.doc:
The belt drive's damping as a ratio of critical damping, stated by whoever knows the belt (a rubber belt on a
carriage rings, about 0.1). Zero is not stated: the belt part's assumed damping (`ASSUMED_DAMPING_RATIO`) is used.

fields.name: DEFAULT_EFFICIENCY
fields.doc: Assumed power efficiency of a timing belt drive.

fields.name: DEFAULT_DRAG
fields.doc: Assumed belt-drive drag at a powered pulley, N m.

fields.name: IDLER_BEARING_DRAG
fields.doc: Assumed rolling-bearing drag at a free idler, N m.

fields.name: ASSUMED_DAMPING_RATIO
fields.doc: The damping of a rubber timing belt, as a ratio of critical damping: a carriage on one rings (assumed, not a datasheet value).

fields.name: twoPulley
fields.doc:
A belt round two pulleys of the same family, a driver at the origin and an idler
`centreDistance` away along +X, both wrapped counter-clockwise.

fields.name: relation
fields.doc: Resolve from the current loop geometry and width, never a saved stiffness.

fields.name: toothClearance
fields.doc: A tooth-clearance allowance at the pitch line, mm, pending measured family data.

fields.name: reduction
fields.doc:
Follower rotation per leader rotation. Power direction belongs to the motor/load, so
the same efficiency applies when the motor is on the follower.

fields.name: freePaths
fields.doc: Free elastic lengths between two engaged pulleys; other wraps turn freely.

fields.name: cordStiffnessPerMm
fields.doc:
Tensile stiffness of the belt's cords, EA in N, per millimetre of belt width. Assumption, not a
datasheet value (makers rate breaking strength and working tension, not stiffness): a 6 mm
GT2 belt with fibreglass cords breaks near 400 N at 2.5% elongation or more, which puts EA
for 6 mm at no more than about 16 kN, so 2500 N per mm of width (15 kN for 6 mm) is on the soft
side of that. Replace it with a measured value for a particular belt.

fields.name: cordRigidityPerWidth
fields.doc: The part carries any profile-specific reference value; geometry never supplies stiffness.

fields.name: assumedWorkingTension
fields.doc: Assumed 2.5% breaking strain with a 1.5 working factor; replace with a belt maker's rating.

fields.name: assumedPretension
fields.doc: Assumed installed tension: 20 N per mm of GT2 width until a tensioner setting is measured.

fields.name: checkTension
fields.doc: A belt under differential pulley force must keep both spans taut and below its working limit.

fields.name: carriageStiffness
fields.doc:
Stiffness at a carriage clamped on strand `strand`, in N/mm of carriage travel, in the worst
place on the strand. The belt is anchored at the driving pulley, so the carriage is held by
two springs in parallel: the free length of the strand between it and the driver (at most the
strand's length, with the carriage at the far end) and the rest of the loop the other way
round. Each is EA over its length, EA from `cordStiffnessPerMm` times the width. Pretension,
tooth compliance and the clamp are left out, so a real belt is a little softer.

fields.name: strands
fields.doc: The straight strands, strand `i` running from wrap `i` to the next.

fields.name: toothLength
fields.doc: Length of the belt as `teeth` whole teeth have it, in millimetres.

fields.name: exactTeeth
fields.doc: The tooth count the length falls at, before it is rounded.

fields.name: slack
fields.doc:
How far a belt of `teeth` whole teeth is longer (positive) or shorter than the loop's pitch
line, in millimetres.

fields.name: centreAdjustment
fields.doc:
How far to move one end pulley of a loop of two parallel runs, along them, to make the loop
exactly `teeth` teeth long: the loop lengthens twice what the centres separate. Positive
moves the pulleys apart.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc:
Which way wrap `wrap` turns about the plane's +Z (+1 counter-clockwise, -1 clockwise) while a
carriage clamped to strand `strand` moves along (`travelX`, `travelY`) in the plane, which
the strand must run along or against.

fields.name: anchorPhase
fields.doc: Arc phase held by a stationary driving pulley, halfway through its contact.

fields.name: anchorDistance
fields.doc: Distance from the start of strand 0 to a material point held on a driving pulley.

fields.name: clampDistanceAt
fields.doc: Distance to the unique straight span containing a physical clamp. A tangent is a wrap.

fields.name: clampDistance
fields.doc: Distance along a specified straight span; callers can derive that span with `clampDistanceAt`.

fields.name: pointAt
fields.doc:
The pitch line at `distance` along the belt, from where strand 0 leaves its wrap, wrapping
round at the belt's length. Without `target`, returns an independent snapshot.
Display mesh builders may pass their own target to reuse its storage.

fields.name: pairRecipeType
fields.doc: Belt round a driver and an idler, in plain tooth counts and a centre distance.

types.name: TimingBeltMesh
types.doc: A display mesh along the posed pitch line; phase is belt travel in millimetres.

types.name: TimingBeltProfile
types.doc:
Belt family and pitch-line geometry for a simplified timing pulley.
Custom requires an explicit family, pitch and pitch-line differential in millimetres.

types.name: TimingPulley
types.doc:
Timing belt pulley with an explicit belt family and a simplified tooth outline. The
groove is a straight-flank preview, not a belt manufacturer's tooth profile. The pitch line
lies in the belt cords outside the pulley, so OD = pitch diameter - 2 * PLD.

types.name: ToothOutline
types.doc:
A closed planar tooth outline (at z = 0) built from its true pieces: splines through sampled involutes,
arcs on tip and root circles, and straight lines. Unlike a polyline through samples, a flank is then one
smooth face, so shading and edge display show the tooth, not its sampling. Pieces must join end to start;
`close` checks that the outline returns to its first point.

fields.name: arc
fields.doc: A circular arc from `start` through `middle` to `end`.

fields.name: spline
fields.doc: An interpolating spline through `points`, in order.

fields.name: close
fields.doc: The closed wire. The pieces are consumed.

fields.name: extrude
fields.doc: The outline extruded along +Z from z0 to z1: a ruled loft between two copies, so every piece becomes one face.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: The placement of a section at height `z`, turned by `angle` radians about +Z.

types.name: TransmissionComponents
types.doc: The transmission package's component recipes.

types.name: TransmissionDesignError
types.doc: Parts are valid individually but cannot work together in this transmission.

types.name: TransmissionRelation
types.doc: Resolved motion and engineering allowances, in the coupling's units.

fields.name: dampingRatio
fields.doc: How damped the coupling's response is, as a ratio of critical damping (of a coupling with a stiffness); the part states it.

fields.name: assumed
fields.doc: Assumptions are a projection of the field bases, so a stated override removes its label.

fields.name: assumptions
fields.doc: Assumption labels stay attached to the field that uses them.

types.name: TransmissionResolver
types.doc: Resolve a saved source against the assembly's current members.

fields.name: mapSource
fields.doc: Keep member references with an included or extracted assembly's namespace.

types.name: ValueBasis
types.doc: Where an engineering value comes from; the IDs are part of the wire schema.

types.name: ArcTorchFacet
types.doc:
An arc torch: `tcpConnector` is the wire tip at nominal stickout with +Z along the wire out of the torch,
`controlPort` is the signal inlet that starts and stops the arc, and `stickoutMm` is that stickout: the
wire's extension past the contact tip, which the arc model needs.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: The facet of this kind on `component`, or null.

types.name: GasCylinder
types.doc:
Shielding gas cylinder with its regulator: a 50 litre steel bottle 1.2 m tall.

CAD frame: standing on its base at z=0 on the origin, the regulator on top. Connector: `base`
(+Y along +Z). Port: the regulated `gas` outlet.

fields.name: mixture
fields.doc: What the bottle holds, such as "Ar/CO2 82/18".

types.name: JointType
types.doc: How the two members of a seam meet, found from the faces' geometry (see `WeldSeams`).

fields.name: Fillet
fields.doc: One member stands on the other's face, with its contact face the narrower (a T-joint).

fields.name: Lap
fields.doc: One member lies on the other's face, with its contact face the wider, so its edge is the corner.

fields.name: Butt
fields.doc: Two end faces meet edge to edge and the outer faces run on flat.

fields.name: Corner
fields.doc: Two end faces meet edge to edge and the outer faces turn (a mitred or square corner).

types.name: RecipeWire
types.doc: The wire a recipe is made for: what the feeder in the CAD declares (its `WireFeed` capability).

types.name: SeamCandidate
types.doc: A seam before it is named and given its process settings.

types.name: SeamChain
types.doc: Seams that join end to end, in welding order and each turned to run on from the one before.

types.name: SeamEdge
types.doc: One edge of a member's B-rep, for seam finding.

fields.name: faces
fields.doc: The two faces that meet along the edge, as indices into the member's faces.

types.name: SeamFace
types.doc: One face of a seam: a member occurrence and the face's topological name in that member's geometry.

types.name: SeamFrame
types.doc:
The pose a torch holds at one place on a seam. All vectors are unit and expressed in the frame the
seam is in (the workpiece's, until `transformed` moves it).

fields.name: tangent
fields.doc: The direction of travel along the seam.

fields.name: bisector
fields.doc: Bisector of the two faces' outward normals, pointing out of the corner: the torch axis at 0 work and travel angle.

fields.name: torchAxis
fields.doc: The torch's axis after the work and travel angles, from the wire tip back toward the torch body.

fields.name: wire
fields.doc: The direction the wire points, from the torch toward the work.

fields.name: toAssemblyFrame
fields.doc:
The wire tip's pose for a robot: +Z along the wire (the torch connector's convention), +X along the direction of
travel as far as it is square to the wire, and Y completing the right-handed frame.

fields.name: transformed
fields.doc: This frame in the parent of the frame it is in now, with `frame` its pose there.

types.name: SeamMember
types.doc: A member's geometry for seam finding: its occurrence id and its part, in the frame the seams are to be found in. Borrowed.

types.name: SeamSolid
types.doc: A member's faces and edges with their adjacency, read once from its part.

types.name: SeamSurface
types.doc: One face of a member's B-rep, for seam finding.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The outward normal and a point on the face; only planar faces take part in seams.

fields.name: loops
fields.doc: The edge indices of each boundary loop, and which loop is the outer one.

fields.name: chords
fields.doc: Every boundary edge as a chord, all loops together: curved edges are sampled.

fields.name: outline
fields.doc: Chords of the outer loop only.

types.name: TorchPlace
types.doc: Where the torch is and which way its wire points: a place a weld starts or ends at, in the workpiece's frame (millimetres).

types.name: WeldAccess
types.doc:
Whether a seam can be welded where the weldment stands: reachable by the robot with the torch at the seam's frames, and the
torch and arm clear of the workpiece, fixtures, table and equipment (but for the wire tip at the seam). It belongs to
whoever knows the robot and its cell, so the generator asks it per seam and does not know how it decides.

fields.name: problem
fields.doc: Why `seam` (welded in the direction it is given) cannot be welded, or null when it can.

types.name: WeldContactSelection
types.doc: Bridge saved nominal CAD patches to measured registration and checked arm probe preparation.

types.name: WeldJoint
types.doc: A joint the weldment says is welded: two members, and how the weld is to be made.

types.name: WeldMetal
types.doc:
The weld metal of a weldment. Before any welding there is none, so in the model it is a speck, a 1 mm cube at the
workpiece's origin that is mated to the workpiece and weighs what that much steel does: the body that carries the
bead. A simulated welder lays its bead on this part at run time, as runtime geometry, so the weld metal is what the
torch actually deposited, not a shape drawn into the model; a real weld would add its mass to this part.

CAD frame: the cube stands on z=0, centred over its origin. Connector `base` (z=0, to mate to the workpiece).

fields.name: carrierOf
fields.doc:
The occurrence that carries the bead of `weldment` in `assembly`: the weld metal part mated to the weldment's reference
member. It is found, not named, so the mission follows whatever the CAD calls it and where it is; a weldment with no
weld metal, or with two, is an error.

types.name: WeldProbeFace
types.doc: A polygonal CAD face available to touch sensing, expressed in the weldment reference frame.

fields.name: contains
fields.doc: Even-odd contours include all holes. A positive inset keeps probes off every boundary.

fields.name: containsRegion
fields.doc: Conservatively contain a complete rectangular uncertainty patch, including holes and concavities.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: A finite search lattice comes from face bounds, never authored weldment coordinates.

types.name: WeldProbeGeometry
types.doc: CAD-only contact patches and nominal visibility; runtime owns reach, motion and observations.

fields.name: contactFaces
fields.doc: Persist CAD-derived boundaries in metres; no live work pose or contact result is included.

fields.name: fromContactFaces
fields.doc: Reconstruct polygonal probe geometry from a validated contact job, without reopening CAD solids.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: Borrowed parts already posed in a common reference frame. Curved boundaries are deliberately unsupported.

fields.name: findIn
fields.doc: Collect actual B-rep faces in the weldment frame, with optional table/clamp obstruction geometry.

fields.name: exposedRegion
fields.doc: Conservative obstruction mask over a full uncertain approach prism, rather than its centre ray.

fields.name: exposed
fields.doc: The outward approach segment may not cross another CAD face or a mating surface.

types.name: WeldProbeObservedBounds
types.doc: Bind observed uncertainty without making CAD geometry depend on a runtime registration implementation.

types.name: WeldProbeParkingBounds
types.doc: Parking error rotates about the chassis origin, not about the workpiece or the arm mount.

types.name: WeldProbePatterns
types.doc: Select geometrically observable contact patterns from patches large enough for the current uncertainty.

types.name: WeldProbeRegionBounds
types.doc: Conservative plane-intersection uncertainty in the CAD model's length unit.

types.name: WeldProbeStage
types.doc: A CAD-derived stage of a 3–2–1 registration sequence, before arm-motion feasibility checks.

types.name: WeldProbeUncertainty
types.doc: Search-ray intersection bounds in the CAD model's length unit, for the current probe placement.

types.name: WeldRun
types.doc: One weld of the mission: seams that run on from one another, in the order and direction they are welded.

fields.name: closed
fields.doc: The last seam ends where the first begins (a tube's perimeter).

fields.name: entry
fields.doc: Where the torch starts the run, and where it ends it.

types.name: WeldSeam
types.doc:
A weld seam found where two members meet: a straight edge between a face of each, in the frame of the
workpiece. It is never authored. The faces are named by their topological names, so the seam keeps
its name, and follows its edge, as the members are edited.

The torch frame comes from the geometry. The tangent runs along the edge; the torch axis is the
bisector of the two faces' outward normals (the open side of the corner), then tilted by the work angle
about the tangent and by the travel angle about the work-angled axis. A positive travel angle pushes
(the wire points ahead of the torch, in the direction of travel); a negative one drags. A positive work
angle leans the axis toward the first face's side.

fields.name: PUSH_ANGLE
fields.doc: Default push angle for MIG welding, in radians.

fields.name: a
fields.doc: `a` and `b` are ordered by member then face name, so the same pair always gives the same seam name.

fields.name: normalA
fields.doc: The faces' outward normals, along the seam.

fields.name: legSize
fields.doc: Intended leg size in millimetres: how far the weld reaches along each face.

fields.name: piece
fields.doc: Which of several seams between the same two faces this is, in order along the faces; 0 when there is one.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (a:SeamFace, b:SeamFace, joint:JointType, start:Vector, stop:Vector, normalA:Vector, normalB:Vector, legSize:Float, passes:Int, travelAngle:Float, workAngle:Float, ?piece:Int):Void

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The seam's name: its two faces, `member:face|member:face`, then `~n` when the faces meet in several seams.

fields.name: centre
fields.doc: Midpoint of the seam.

fields.name: normalAngle
fields.doc: Angle between the two faces' outward normals, in radians: 90 degrees for a square corner, 0 for a butt.

fields.name: bisector
fields.doc: The torch axis with no work and travel angle: out of the corner, between the two faces.

fields.name: reversed
fields.doc: The seam welded the other way: from its stop to its start. The name is the same.

fields.name: configured
fields.doc: The same seam with other process settings; an argument left out keeps its value.

fields.name: frameAt
fields.doc: The torch frame `distance` along the seam from its start, clamped to the seam.

fields.name: frameAtParameter
fields.doc: The torch frame at `fraction` of the way along the seam, 0 at the start and 1 at the stop.

fields.name: transformed
fields.doc: This seam in the parent of the frame it is in now, with `frame` its pose there.

types.name: WeldSeams
types.doc:
Finds weld seams where two members meet, from their geometry alone.

Two kinds of contact are looked for, both between planar faces:
- **Edge on face (fillet, lap).** An edge of one member lies on a face of the other, and the member's face
that holds that edge lies flat against it (opposite normals). That face is the contact; the member's
other face on the edge is the side face. The seam is the stretch of that edge where the other member's
face continues past it, on the side the side face looks toward: the open side of the corner. Where the
face stops (a flush end, or the edge of a plate), there is no corner and so no seam. Only edges on the
contact face's outer boundary count, so the inside of a hollow section is left alone. The joint is a
fillet when the contact is narrower than the side face is tall (a T-joint) and a lap when it is wider.
- **Edge to edge (butt, corner).** An edge of each member coincides, and the faces on either side that
meet flat against each other are the contact. The seam is the groove the two other faces make.

Each seam runs between one face of each member, named by the two faces' topological names. A tube
section's perimeter is one seam per side, since each side lies between a different pair of faces;
`chains` joins the sides that run on from one another.

fields.name: TOUCH
fields.doc: Two surfaces this close are touching, in millimetres: a bigger gap is a gap, not a seam.

fields.name: find
fields.doc:
The seams between members `a` and `b`, in the frame their parts are in. Each carries the leg size, passes and
angles given. A pair that doesn't touch has none, so the result is empty.

fields.name: chains
fields.doc:
Groups seams into chains of seams that meet end to end, as around a tube's perimeter. Each chain is in welding order
and each seam is turned to run on from the one before; the first keeps its direction. `closed` is set for a loop.

types.name: WeldingControlInterface
types.doc: How a controller drives a welding power source.

fields.name: AnalogIo
fields.doc: Trigger and enable on digital I/O, setpoints as 0-10 V.

fields.name: ModbusTcp
fields.doc: Registers over Modbus TCP.

types.name: WeldingEquipment
types.doc:
Reads the welding equipment of an assembly from its parts' capabilities and its connections.

Grounded work is derived, never listed: the power source's work lead (`weldNegative`) is traced
to the work clamp it is connected to, and the clamp's mates say what it sits on. The weld
circuit returns through that member and through every member welded to it (a `Weldment`'s
members are one conductor: welded joints carry current, and a seam's two sides are the same
metal). A mate does not make a conductor: a workpiece lying on a table is positioned there, not
bonded to it, so the table stays outside the circuit unless the clamp is on the table.

fields.name: of
fields.doc:
The equipment of `assembly`, which has exactly one power source whose work lead reaches a work
clamp, and a wire feeder. `weldments` are the welded workpieces in the assembly's own ids.

types.name: WeldingEquipmentData
types.doc: What a welding robot's simulated or real welder needs to know about the cell around its torch.

types.name: WeldingInterfaces
types.doc:
The service interfaces welding equipment shares, so a torch, feeder, power source and cylinder
mate only through the connections a real set-up has.

fields.name: mains
fields.doc: Mains cord: line, neutral and earth.

types.name: WeldingMission
types.doc:
The mission that welds a whole weldment, generated from the seams its declared joints have (`Weldment.find`), so that adding
a member adds its seams. Nothing in it is authored: the seams come from the members' geometry, the process from the leg and
the wire (`WeldingRecipe`), and what a seam needs of the robot is asked of a `WeldAccess`.

- **One step per run.** `WeldSeams.chains` joins the sides that meet end to end (a tube's four sides), and each chain is one
`weld` step, welded with the arc up from corner to corner. A chain whose seams ask for different legs is split where the
leg changes, since a step has one process.
- **Order.** The runs are ordered to keep the torch from travelling and turning through the air: a greedy nearest-neighbour
tour. From where the torch is (`home`, the ready pose) the next run is the one, and the way of welding it, whose start is
nearest to where the torch ended, measured as the distance between the two places plus `TURN_COST` millimetres per radian
of the angle between the two wire directions (reorienting the torch is slower than moving it). The way of welding is each
run's choice of direction (the run, or its seams, reversed) and, for a closed run, of the corner it starts at. A greedy
tour is not the shortest, but the runs of a weldment are few and the cost is only the air time between them; the tour
and its totals are reported (`airTravel`, `turned`) so that a better order can be told from a worse.
- **Every seam must be weldable.** A joint with no seam, a seam of a joint type that is not deposited yet (only fillets
are), and a seam the robot cannot reach or cannot weld clear of the work are errors in `diagnostics`, each naming the seam
and why, and the mission is then not generated (`steps` is empty; `require` throws). The weldment is the cell's own CAD,
which we can change, so a joint that cannot be welded is a fault in the design to be fixed, not something to skip silently
and weld around. A seam is judged in both directions it can be welded in: it is unweldable only if neither works.

fields.name: TURN_COST
fields.doc: Millimetres of air travel one radian of torch reorientation costs.

fields.name: airTravel
fields.doc: The length of the moves between runs, from `home`, in millimetres, and the angle the wire turns over them, in radians.

fields.name: require
fields.doc: The steps, or an exception listing every seam that could not be welded and why.

fields.name: generate
measure
fields.doc: The air travel between runs from `home`, in millimetres, and the angle the wire turns over those moves, in radians.

types.name: WeldingPassRecipe
types.doc: A pass's settings and tip offset along the CAD face normals, in millimetres.

types.name: WeldingPowerSource
types.doc:
Single-phase MIG/MAG power source for robot welding. It runs from 230 V mains, passes the
shielding gas through to the feeder, and takes its trigger and setpoints from the robot's
controller.

CAD frame: a box centred over its origin in X and Y, standing on its base at z=0, front toward
+Y. Connector: `base` (+Y along +Z). Ports: the `mains` inlet, the `gas` inlet and `control`
inlet, the weld output sockets `weldPositive` (to the feeder) and `weldNegative` (the work
lead), and the pass-throughs `gasOut` and `feederControl`.

fields.name: WORK_LEAD
fields.doc: The port the work lead leaves by, which the work clamp's lead plugs into.

fields.name: efficiency
fields.doc: Arc power delivered per watt drawn from the mains: about 0.88 for an inverter source.

types.name: WeldingProcess
types.doc: An arc process a welding power source can run.

fields.name: Mig
fields.doc: Gas metal arc with an inert shielding gas.

fields.name: Mag
fields.doc: Gas metal arc with an active shielding gas, such as argon with CO2.

types.name: WeldingRecipe
types.doc:
How a weld is run, derived from the seam and the wire: the settings of a MIG fillet in solid steel wire that lay a leg
of the size the weldment asks for. Nothing in it is a seam's geometry; that comes from the CAD (`WeldSeam`). The
recipe is the generator's inverse of what the simulated welder does: it picks a wire speed for the leg, the voltage
that goes with it, and the travel speed at which that wire speed deposits the cross-section of an equal-leg fillet,
`area = leg² / 2`. It assumes the wire's deposition efficiency, which the CAD gives with the wire. The leg the weld then
reaches is measured, not derived: the player compares the bead the welder laid with the leg asked for, so a wrong
efficiency, a wire that is not the one assumed, or a torch that does not hold the speed shows as a leg that is off.

- The wire speed grows with the leg (`1.5 · leg + 0.5` metres per minute, clamped), and must be one the feeder can
feed: a leg that needs more is refused.
- The voltage follows the wire speed on a synergic line, `15 + 1.1 · wire speed` volts, rounded to half a volt.
- The travel speed is `wire speed · wire area · efficiency / area`.

types.name: WeldingSupplyFacet
types.doc: A welding power source: the processes it runs, its rated current in amperes, how a controller drives it, and its efficiency (the fraction of the mains power it delivers to the arc).

fields.name: of
fields.doc: The facet of this kind on `component`, or null.

types.name: WeldingTorch
types.doc:
Robot MIG torch: a breakaway mount, a straight handle, a swan neck bent 22 or 45 degrees, a gas
nozzle and a contact tip, 360 mm from mount to wire tip. The component is the mount and the handle; the swan
neck with its elbow is `WeldingTorchNeck`, mated to the `neck` connector at the bend, and the nozzle with the contact tip
is `WeldingTorchNozzle` on the neck's end, so that each is a convex body of its own for collision (a hull around the whole
bent torch would fill in the crook of the neck, and around the neck and nozzle together the step between their radii).

CAD frame: the mount face at z=0 and the handle along +Z; the neck bends toward +X, so the
nozzle points along (sin bend, 0, cos bend). Connectors: `robot` (the mount face, mate it to the
tool plate's `tool`, +Y along +Z like every tool mount) and `tcp` (the wire tip at the nominal
stickout past the contact tip, with +Z along the wire out of the torch). Ports: the weld
`power` cable, `gas`, the `wire` liner and the `control` signal that starts the arc, all inlets
supplied through the feeder.

The breakaway mount is the torch's own base: a spring-loaded collar that lets go in a crash.
Geometry is solid, square-shouldered stock, so the torch is its own collision shape.

fields.name: MOUNT_LENGTH
fields.doc:
The breakaway collar, the straight handle, the neck, the nozzle and the tip's reach beyond the
nozzle, along their axes. The bend sits at the end of the handle.

fields.name: STICKOUT
fields.doc: Wire past the contact tip when the arc is lit.

fields.name: MASS
fields.doc: The torch's mass, kg, and the neck's part of it.

fields.name: bendDegrees
fields.doc: Neck bend from the handle's axis, in degrees: 22 or 45.

fields.name: NECK_R
fields.doc: The radii of the neck's parts, for `WeldingTorchNeck`.

fields.name: wireDirection
fields.doc: Direction the wire leaves the torch in, in the torch's frame.

types.name: WeldingTorchNeck
types.doc:
The swan neck of a robot MIG torch (`WeldingTorch`): the elbow at the bend and the neck, along +Z of its own frame.
It is mated to the torch's `neck` connector, which puts +Z along the nozzle's axis. Its own part, so that its collision
shape is the neck and not a hull around the whole bent torch.

CAD frame: the elbow's centre at the origin, the neck along +Z. Connectors: `base` (the elbow's centre) and `nozzle` (the
neck's end, where `WeldingTorchNozzle` is mated).

types.name: WeldingTorchNozzle
types.doc:
The gas nozzle and contact tip of a robot MIG torch (`WeldingTorch`), along +Z of its own frame, mated to the end of the
swan neck (`WeldingTorchNeck`). Its own part, so that its collision shape is the nozzle and not a hull around the step
from the neck's radius to the nozzle's.

CAD frame: the nozzle's base at the origin, the tip pointing along +Z. Connector `base`.

types.name: Weldment
types.doc:
The welded joints of a workpiece. It names the members that make up the workpiece and the pairs of them
that are welded, with the leg size and passes for each. It does not say where: the seams come from the
members' geometry (`WeldSeams`), so they follow the members as they are edited and a pair that does not
touch is reported rather than skipped.

The seams are expressed in the workpiece's own frame, the pose of its `reference` member. A robot's
program gets the seam frames there and places them with the workpiece's pose in the world, so a
correction to that pose (the part lay a little off, or touch sensing found it) moves every seam.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: The member whose pose is the workpiece's frame.

fields.name: members
fields.doc: Occurrence ids of the members.

fields.name: join
fields.doc: Declares that members `a` and `b` are welded, with a leg of `legSize` millimetres in `passes` passes.

fields.name: prefixed
fields.doc: The same weldment for an assembly that includes the workpiece under `prefix`, such as `work/`.

fields.name: find
fields.doc:
Finds the seams of every declared joint in the members' parts (by occurrence id, in the world), expressed in the
frame of `workpiece`, the reference member's pose, when given. The parts are borrowed. A joint whose members do
not touch gives an error naming them and the gap between their bounds.

fields.name: findIn
fields.doc:
Finds the seams in an assembly that contains the members, from their geometry at `poses` (`assembly.solvedPoses()`,
or the state a robot is simulated in). They come out in the workpiece's frame, so they stay put when the
workpiece is moved as a whole.

types.name: WeldmentSeams
types.doc: What `Weldment.find` found: the seams, and an error for every declared joint that has none.

fields.name: require
fields.doc: The seams, or an exception listing every joint that could not be found.

fields.name: named
fields.doc: The seam with that name, or null.

fields.name: between
fields.doc: The seams between two members, whichever order they were declared in.

types.name: WireFeedFacet
types.doc: A wire feeder: the diameter of the wire it feeds in millimetres, its top wire speed in metres per minute, and the fraction of the wire that ends up in the weld.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: The facet of this kind on `component`, or null.

types.name: WireFeeder
types.doc:
Wire feeder for a robot torch: a closed box with the wire spool and drive rolls inside. It
takes weld current, shielding gas and control from the power source and passes them, with the
wire, on to the torch.

CAD frame: a box centred over its origin in X and Y, standing on its base at z=0. Connector:
`mount` (the base, +Y along +Z). Ports: `power`, `gas` and `control` inlets, and the supplies
`torchPower`, `torchGas`, `torchControl` and `torchWire`.

fields.name: wireDiameterMm
fields.doc:
The wire it feeds, in millimetres, and its top speed in metres per minute. `depositionEfficiency` is the fraction of
the melted wire that reaches the weld (the rest is spatter and fume): a property of the wire and its shielding gas,
which `SOLID_WIRE_EFFICIENCY` gives for solid steel wire in argon-CO2. The weld recipe and the simulated weld both take
it from here, through the scene's torch block.

types.name: WorkClamp
types.doc:
Magnetic work clamp: the return of the weld circuit. The arc closes through the workpiece
and back by the work lead, so a workpiece the clamp is not on cannot be welded.

It is a magnet block that sits on a steel face of the workpiece, with the lead's lug on its
side: a robot cell's work lead goes to the workpiece, not to the table it lies on, because the
contact between a loose part and its table (scale, paint, a thin edge) is not a dependable
conductor, and a magnet needs no re-clamping for each part.

CAD frame: standing on its contact face at z=0, centred over its origin in X and Y. Connector:
`contact` (the face, +Y along +Z: mate it to the workpiece). Port: the `lead` inlet, the end
of the work lead from the power source.

types.name: WorkReturnFacet
types.doc: A work clamp, the return of the weld circuit: `leadPort` is the inlet the work lead from the power source plugs into, and `contactConnector` is where the clamp meets the work (mate it to the workpiece).

fields.name: of
fields.doc: The facet of this kind on `component`, or null.
